ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募參與者：社交焦慮短期介入訓練計劃
六週指導式自助練習，處理社會評價與自我批評
打破自我批評的惡性循環
找回自我肯定的正向情緒
📍
香港中文大學校園內，全程免費
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊現正推行一項針對社交焦慮問題的短期介入訓練計劃，誠邀符合資格的人士參與。
社交焦慮不止影響我們如何應對社交場合，亦關乎我們如何看待自己，以及如何與他人建立聯繫。目前，社交焦慮問題的治療多採用認知行為取向，研究證實能有效改善個人在社交情境中的功能表現。本計劃則是團隊基於實證研究開發的新訓練方案，採用社會情緒取向，聚焦於處理個人與自我及他人的關係。本項目遵循階梯式照護模式 (stepped-care model)，定位為指導式自助 (guided self-help) 短期介入方案，旨在以較少的時間投入及心理負擔，為參加者提供有效支援。
訓練為期6週，包括「每週1次實體會面 + 自助練習 + 線上心理評估訪談及問卷」 ； 訓練完成後1個月和六個月進行隨訪評估
📢 「招募要求」
年滿18歲或以上；廣東話流利；
在社交焦慮方面感到困擾，例如在社交或公開場合強烈緊張焦慮、擔心自己被負面評價、迴避社交場合，並明顯影響工作或學習；
現時並未接受其他形式的心理治療或精神科藥物治療；
能夠親身前往香港中文大學校園參與訓練。
🔗
「參與流程」
報名後，我們將聯絡您安排篩選問卷及訪談，以確認是否適合參加本計劃，並邀請符合條件者參與訓練。
🔗
「報名連結」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
如有疑問，歡迎聯絡研究團隊：cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
本計劃已獲香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會審批（CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796）。
所有個人資料僅用作研究篩選及介入用途，並會嚴格保密。
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
Recruiting Participants: Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a brief intervention programme for individuals experiencing social anxiety difficulties. We invite eligible individuals to participate.
Social anxiety not only affects how we cope in social situations but also involves how we view ourselves and relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural approaches are widely used and evidence-based for treating social anxiety, our team has developed a novel training protocol grounded in empirical research that adopts a social-emotional approach, focusing on improving individuals’ relationships with themselves and with others. Following the stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, aiming to provide effective support with minimal time commitment and psychological burden.
The training programme spans 6 weeks and includes:
Weekly in-person sessions (once per week)
Self-help practice exercises
Questionnaire assessments
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted one month and six months after the training.
「Eligibility Criteria」
Aged 18 or above
Fluent in Cantonese
Experiencing significant social anxiety-related distress (e.g., intense anxiety in social or public settings, fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of social situations, with noticeable impact on work or study)
Not currently receiving other forms of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication
Able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus
「Procedures」
After registration, we will contact you to arrange a screening questionnaire and an interview to determine your suitability for the programme. Eligible participants will then be invited to join the training.
「Registration Link」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
For enquiries, please contact our research team at: cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796).
All personal data collected will be used solely for research screening and intervention purposes and will be kept strictly confidential.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

- English is your first/native and dominant language

From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Ever needed to compare two versions of a document and dreaded the tedious side-by-side reading? 😩 Upload
both versions
into
M365 Copilot
and let it do the detective work! It will highlight differences, additions, and removals in seconds.
📋 Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
"I've uploaded two versions of our handbook — the current version and the proposed update. Please: (1) List all sections that were changed, added, or removed, (2) For each change, summarize what was modified and why it might matter, (3) Highlight any changes  (4) Create a change log table with columns: Section, Type of Change, Summary, Impact Level (High/Medium/Low)."
💡 Why this works:
Structuring the comparison as a change log with impact levels turns a tedious manual comparison into an instant, prioritized review. Decision-makers can focus on high-impact changes first!
📑
Use for
: Contract revisions, policy updates, proposal iterations, budget comparisons (upload two Excel files!), or any before/after document review. Saves
hours
of side-by-side reading!
💡More Tips & Resources
Looking for more ways to level up your Copilot game? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

🌟 What are the essential soft skills in the workplace? Co-op@CUHK helps you meet employers’ expectations! 🌟  - Office of Co-operative Education Programme (OCEP)
From: Office of Co-operative Education Programme (OCEP)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
coop@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
🌟
What are the essential soft skills in the workplace?
Co-op@CUHK helps you meet employers’ expectations!
🌟
Have you ever wondered what qualities employers value most? Employers are seeking more than just good grades. Strong soft skills, such as analytical thinking, resilience, flexibility, agility, leadership, and social influence, are essential for success in the workplace. Co-op’s dedicated courses help you develop these important competencies with our preparatory courses.
COOP3001: Unlocking Employability Potential and Personal Branding (1 Unit)
With sessions on understanding oneself through Personality Dimensions, mastering first impressions, career planning and related topics, Co-op students will be able to:
Demonstrate a deeper understanding of their personality, strengths and interests, enabling them to build a distinctive personal brand (
Self-awareness
)
Identify their career aspirations and analyse labour market opportunities to make informed career development plans (
Analytical Thinking
).
Adapt pragmatic strategies to changing workplace expectations (
Flexibility and Agility
).
COOP3002: Developing Workplace Professionalism (2 Units)
Through classes on Excel skills, problem solving in the era of AI, professional email writing, workplace etiquette and together with other experiential learning initiatives such as Outward Bound Training, Co-op students will be able to:
Apply analytical or AI tools effectively to support workplace productivity and decision-making (
Technological Literacy
).
Analyse workplace challenges critically, as well as develop pragmatic and innovative recommendations (
Creative Thinking
)
Communicate professionally through written correspondence and workplace interactions (
Empathy and Active Listening
)
Co-op provides a valuable platform for students to cultivate essential soft skills and better prepare themselves for the challenges at workplace. Application for the 6th cohort is now open! Fill out the
online application form
and join us!
To stay updated with the latest information, follow our Programme on
LinkedIn
and
IG
.

coop@cuhk.edu.hk
or call 3943 5674 / 3943 1422.

誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）
學童家長
學童需以廣東話為母語，並在香港居住 2.5 年以上
目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。
面對面測試在網上測試完成後另約時間進行，約需45分鐘
家長：
在網上測試平台接受
約
15分鐘的語文及數學測試
，及填寫關於學童學習情況與家庭語言環境的
問卷
第二部分（可選擇是否參與）
學童：腦電圖測試（EEG），約2小時
報酬：每年測試完結後將收到：
(1) 測試結果的個人報告；(2) 港幣200元超級市場現金券；(3) 小禮物，
參與腦電圖 (EEG) 部份的學生另有250元超級市場現金券
研究詳情及報名請見以下網頁：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
如對是項研究有任何疑問或查詢，歡迎聯絡本項目的首席研究員Urs Maurer教授（電郵: umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk）或研究小組（電話：3943-4379；電郵：
lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com
）。
We are recruiting for a multi-disciplinary study about the Chinese, English, and Mathematical abilities among Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong. Details are as below:
Target participants:
Singletons and twins (both identical and fraternal) from K3 to P6 in the 2024/25 school year
Students’ parents
The child participant must be a native Cantonese speaker and have lived in Hong Kong for more than 2.5 years.
Content:
Part 1
Students
: A series of assessments on Chinese, English, and mathematics on the project’s online testing platform. The tasks are divided into six portions; each takes about 40 minutes to finish. Online testing can be completed at your own pace, as long as all tasks are completed within 4 weeks.
A follow-up face-to-face session (45 minutes) will be arranged upon completion of the online testing.
Parents
: Short online testing on language and mathematics abilities (15 minutes), as well as a set of questionnaires on children’s learning and home language environment
Part 2 (optional)
Students: electroencephalography (EEG) test (~2 hour)
Rewards: After each round of testing, participants will receive:
(1) Personal performance report; (2) $200 supermarket vouchers; (3) a gift (for students); EEG participants will receive an additional $250 worth of supermarket vouchers

教育心理學系謝志成教授一項關於中文複合詞的研究誠意邀請與會者參與。
對象：
**參加者需為粵語是母語的本港學生；
**參與者需要有良好的視力或矯正視力；
**參與者需慣性用右手。
**參與者年齡需大於18嵗。
研究內容：整個實驗將為期三節（每節之間間隔不超過一星期）進行，每節需要 1 至 1.5 小時，完成3節後可得到250港元作為現金補償。
地點：陳國本樓707E室
參與方式：如有興趣，請點此連結報名https://forms.gle/znR7QB79PVof2F87A

有興趣的同學請提供每週至少兩個時間段，以便安排。
*若閣下沒有收到我們的電郵，代表所選的時間已額滿，多謝！
*若已參加過【對於中文複合詞所表達的情感】的研究，請勿重複報名。
如果對實驗有任何疑問，歡迎聯絡
xicheng3@cuhk.edu.hk

教授中文課程

English Version:
Do you know your child’s traditional Chinese character reading and writing ability? Don’t miss this fun and meaningful research opportunity!
By taking part in this study, your child can not only receive compensation but also bring home a lovely gift!
Study Tasks:
We are inviting Primary 4 students (who have just completed Grade 4 and are about to begin Grade 5) to take part in writing and reading tasks in Traditional Chinese. We will use specialized equipment to record writing trajectories and pressure, and assess reading and language abilities through interactive language games.
Duration:
Approximately 2 hours
Location:
Leung Kau Kui Building (Department of Linguistics), The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Compensation:
Participants will receive HKD 400 in cash, along with a set of Chiikawa stationery gifts 🎁
Eligibility Requirements:
A fourth-grade student (just finished fourth grade and is about to start fifth grade).
Receiving Chinese instruction in Traditional Chinese and Cantonese at school
Normal vision (glasses allowed), with no eye discomfort
Normal hearing
No history of neurological conditions (e.g., brain injury, epilepsy)
Right-handed (e.g., writing and using utensils with the right hand)
Have not participated in related studies of this project (if unsure, please contact the researcher: Miss Rao,
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
)

The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260720)  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 20 July to 24 July: (1) Academic Reading: Strategies for Success, (2) Building a Bigger and Better Vocabulary, (3) Job Preparation Series: Ace Your In-person and Video Job Interviews, and (4) Listening to Learn: Academic Listening and Note-taking Skills. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
20 July (Mon): 14:30 – 16:30
21 July (Tue): 14:30 – 16:30
22 July (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
23 July (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30
24 July (Fri): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 20 July to 24 July: (1) Cantonese Interview Skills, (2) Preparation for the JRE: How to write government official letters, (3) JRE Argumentative Writing I, and (4) An introduction to the ancient Chinese military treatise: Sunzi the Art of War (PTH). These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心七月二十日至七月二十四日舉辦 (1) 粵語面試技巧, (2) 粵語平仄與近體詩及對聯, (3) JRE政府公函寫作, (4) JRE 議論文寫作 (一), (5) 「信而好古」——粵語與中國古代文化 （粵）, 及 (6) 古兵法略說：孫子 (普)等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於七月二十日至七月二十四日提供以下中文輔導時段。
21 July (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
22 July (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
23 July (Thu): 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/EN/index.aspx

香港中文大學現正進行一項有關長者身心健康的調查，從而制定一個可以測量長者健康生活品質的工具。

個人訪問約需時 30-40 分鐘。完成訪問後，長者與照顧者合共可獲港幣 200 元現金以作答謝。每位參加者只限參加一次。

tudy Background
The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting an interview on the physical and mental health of older adults in Hong Kong to develop a tool in measuring their health-related quality of life in Hong Kong.
Target Group
Elderly: Aged 65 or above; Caregiver: 18 years old or above;
Hong Kong residents;
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese; and
Has ever used elderly service facilities or nursing homes.

If you meet the above criteria, please complete the registration form in around 1-3 minutes. After registration, our staff will contact you within two weeks and arrange an in-person interview for you and the elderly participant to complete.

From: Lo Eugene
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
eugenelo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
🛌🌙 招募參與跨文化睡眠研究參加者 🌙🛌 (15分鐘問卷，有機會獲得$100現金券！）
研究概要：
本研究旨在了解不同文化背景下，人們如何理解及詮釋睡眠癱瘓（俗稱「鬼壓床」）及相關睡眠感知經驗。
透過參與本研究，您可以幫助我們了解睡眠習慣、文化信念及感官體驗如何影響人們對這些特殊睡眠經驗的理解，以及不同文化之間的差異。
本研究由杜倫大學（Durham University）與香港中文大學心理學系合作進行。
參加資格：
• 18歲或以上人士
• 現為英國或香港的大學生
• 具基本閱讀英文的能力
• 沒有神經系統疾病（例如癲癇）
• 沒有藥物或酒精濫用問題
• 不需要曾經歷睡眠癱瘓（鬼壓床）
研究詳情：
參加者需完成一份約15分鐘的網上問卷，內容包括：
• 睡眠癱瘓或相關睡眠經驗
• 睡眠及午睡習慣
• 感官與知覺體驗
• 對超自然或科學解釋的看法
潛在風險：
本研究預期不會有任何潛在風險。
研究回饋：
30位完成問卷者將於九月隨機抽出，每人可獲港幣$100現金券。
所有參與均屬自願性質，所有作答內容將被嚴格保密，並只供研究用途。
如有興趣參與研究，請掃描 QR Code
或填寫問卷連結。
https://durhambs.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gxhPknKBxTHAQS
如對本研究有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡：
Mr. Lee Yau Wai
dhhl12@durham.ac.uk
🛌🌙 Participants Wanted for a Cross-Cultural Sleep Study 🌙🛌
(15-minute questionnaire with a chance to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher!)
Research Overview:
This study aims to explore how people from different cultural backgrounds understand and interpret sleep paralysis (commonly referred to as the “Sleep Paralysis Demon” or “Ghost Oppression”) and related sleep-related perceptual experiences.
By participating in this study, you can help us better understand how sleep habits, cultural beliefs, and sensory experiences influence people’s interpretations of these unusual sleep experiences across cultures.
This research is conducted collaboratively by Durham University and the Department of Psychology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Eligibility:
• Aged 18 or above
• Currently a university student in the UK or Hong Kong
• Able to read English
• No neurological disorders (e.g. epilepsy)
• No drug or alcohol abuse problems
• You do not need to have experienced sleep paralysis before
Study Details:
Participants will complete an online questionnaire that takes approximately 15 minutes. The questionnaire includes:
• Sleep paralysis or related sleep experiences
• Sleep and napping habits
• Sensory and perceptual experiences
• Beliefs about supernatural or scientific explanations
Potential risk:
No potential risks are anticipated in the study.
Participant Reward:
30 participants who complete the questionnaire will be randomly selected in September to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher.
Participation in this study is entirely voluntary. All responses will be kept strictly confidential and used for research purposes only.

Dear Students,
You are cordially invited to participate in a survey study jointly led by Prof. Emmanuel Cheung (Critical Care Medicine Unit, University of Hong Kong) and Dr. Ann Lau (Centre for Bioethics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong).
As you may be aware, the Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance will come into effect on 31 July 2026. This study seeks to explore medical students’ knowledge and preparedness to engage in advance care planning and end-of-life discussions.

招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants Ms. Chan or Mr. Meng.

賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 現誠邀60歲以上人士參加一項靜觀課程研究
研究將會探討靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群的影響。
很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;
iv) 照顧者負荷指數達 7分或以上;
v)沒有經醫生診斷有精神病患或認知問題;
vi) 沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題;
vi)不是正接受心理治療;
vii) 兩年內沒有參加過正規的靜觀課程;
viii) 被照顧親屬並非剛離世;
ix) 三個月內沒有使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間：8月中開始 星期一或二的 上午
地點：沙田瀝源健康院 - 本活動共8節, 每週1次, 每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，及結束後3個月填寫共次3問卷調查及提供3次糞便樣本。
*費用全免*
參與是次研究不需繳付任何費用。
每次提供樣本及填寫問卷將會獲得價值$100 的現金卷，最高可獲300元現金卷。
歡迎將以上資訊廣傳給親朋好友。

Want
M365 Copilot
to nail it on the first try? 🎯 The secret is
constraints
! Adding specific limits — word count, format, audience level, do/don’t rules — dramatically improves the output. Think of constraints as guardrails that keep Copilot on the exact road you want.
📋 Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
“Write a safety reminder announcement for our warehouse team about proper lifting techniques. Constraints: (1) Maximum 100 words, (2)
Writing style: Clear and simple
, (3) Include exactly 3 key safety tips, (4) End with a memorable safety slogan, (5) Do NOT use technical terminology, (6) Format as a poster-ready text with a bold title.”
💡 Why this works:
Each constraint acts like a guardrail — the more specific your boundaries, the less guesswork Copilot has to do, and the closer the output matches your exact needs.
🧪
Bonus tip:
Useful constraints to try: “Use bullet points only”, “Write for a non-technical audience”, “Keep each paragraph under 3 sentences”, “Include a call to action”, “Use active voice only.”

「重塑榕樹凹：共創山海村落」—
地方營造大使招募
中文大學建築學院現正推動一項以「鄉郊地方營造（Rural Placemaking）」為核心的鄉村學堂及暑期工作坊，誠邀熱愛香港鄉郊文化、樂於親身參與實作的你，一同走進榕樹凹，參與村落景觀的復育與共創行動。
計劃期間，我們將邀請香港建造學院團隊擔任導師，帶領參加者學習傳統建造工藝及鄉郊實踐技術。參加者可自選出席一天或多天工作坊。若完成九天的工作坊後，參加者將獲頒由中文大學建築學院及香港建造學院簽發之服務證書，以作嘉許。
榕樹凹介紹：
榕樹凹位於新界東北端，於三百多年前開基立村，是一條歷史悠久的客家溫姓村落，村落鼎盛時期曾有逾三百名居民。由於地理位置接近邊境，榕樹凹在1980年代曾設有英軍軍營，留下了一段獨特而鮮為人知的歷史印記。雖然村落現已無人居住，但村民近年積極推動復村工作，透過修復祖屋、整理村史、舉辦村宴及傳統儀式，如籌辦麒麟隊；重建社群連結與文化記憶，展現出對深厚的鄉土感情與文化傳承精神。
****************************************
願景
共創鄉郊地方營造：以低碳修復與地方記憶，重塑山海景觀。
空間實作：以小型建設改善路徑與休憩空間。
感官敘事：將歷史轉化為具體的景觀導覽。
​共創行動：透過行動連結設計思考與鄉村振興。
****************************************

****************************************

物資收集：在山海與村落之間收集可用材料。
景觀實踐*：進行場地清理及空間建設實作，由香港建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂，教授鄉郊景觀實踐技藝與傳統建造方法。
（ * 代表當日將由建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂及景觀實踐活動。）

“Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.
Sensory Narratives
Transforming local history into tangible landscape interpretation experiences.
Collective Action
Connecting design thinking with rural revitalisation through practical engagement.
Venue:
Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok, New Territories
Programme Format and Phases
Village Guided Tour
Understanding the history of Yung Shue Au and learning about rural placemaking and cultural landscapes.
Material Collection
Collecting usable materials from the surrounding mountain, coastal, and village environment.
Landscape Practice
Participating in site clearing and spatial construction workshops led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction, focusing on rural landscape practices and traditional building techniques.

This includes the potential to increase or decrease the number of sessions. Registered participants will be notified directly of any changes, and updates will be posted across our promotional platforms.

2. During the project period, all boat transportation costs related to the workshops will be arranged and subsidised by the project. Participants are responsible for their own land transportation and should prepare sufficient food and drinking water.
3. The workshops will be conducted in Cantonese.
4. Workshop arrangements may be adjusted due to weather, road conditions, project progress, or the physical conditions of participants and staff without prior notice.
5. The workshops involve physical labour and extended outdoor activities. Participants with health conditions, previous injuries, or physical discomfort are advised to inform the organisers in advance.
6. There are no shops or supply facilities in the village. Participants should prepare sufficient drinking water, sun protection, mosquito repellent, and rain gear if necessary.
7. Mosquitoes and insects are common at the workshop site. Participants are advised to wear light-coloured long-sleeved clothing and long trousers, and bring insect repellent if needed.
8. Basic third-party liability insurance is included. Participants may arrange additional insurance at their own discretion.
9. Rural paths may be uneven, slippery, or covered with loose gravel. Participants should walk carefully.
10. The organisers reserve the right to terminate participation if safety instructions or staff arrangements are not followed.
11. Photographs and/or video recordings may be taken during the activities for documentation, reporting, publicity, and promotional purposes. Participants who do not wish to appear in photographs or recordings should inform staff before the activity begins.

Multicultural Psychological Support Service: Counselling Service for Non-Local Students
No matter where we come from, we all desire to express our emotional needs with no barrier. Speaking in our mother tongue with someone who shares our cultural background not only allows us to better articulate ourselves but also fosters a deeper sense of understanding.
In order to support CUHK non-local students, the Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) offers Multicultural Psychological Support Service. This service allows students to receive counselling services in a comfortable environment.
The service is provided by St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service, and it is available to all CUHK full-time non-local students. The counsellors from St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service are capable of providing counselling services in English or Putonghua, as well as other languages including English, Putonghua, French, German, Dutch, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Urdu, Russian, Sindhi and Tagalog (subject to counsellor’s availability). Experience a  novel intervention on insomnia --- come and earn $600 coupon 誠邀失眠患者體驗新型失眠幹預手段，改善失眠，並可獲得$600超市禮券 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Chen Yang, Xie Chen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155249610@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
失眠吃安眠藥都沒用？來試試新方法
，
改善失眠，完成
可獲得600超市禮券
📣📣📣
初步研究已表明在深度睡眠期間播放特殊處理過的低頻聲波，可改善睡眠品質。本研究用於調查聲音刺激是否可顯著改善失眠症狀，招募符合以下條件的人群參與研究：
18至45歲成年人
無嚴重精神障礙疾病
確診患有失眠症（即出現失眠症狀，每週發作至少三次，持續不少於三個月，並對日間工作、學習或社交造成影響）
能閱讀繁體中文或廣東話
研究流程
:
佩戴14天體動手錶和填寫睡眠日記 （前7天和後7天連續，中間空一天）。
於第八日上午前往沙田醫院7樓睡眠研究室，進行全日檢測（認知測試、情緒睡眠評估、問卷填寫）, 當晚接受多導睡眠檢查。聲音刺激有機會在深度睡眠期出現。
翌日早晨出院 （可提供病假紙）。
完成整個研究，即可獲得一份由專家出具的專屬睡眠報告同600 HKD的購物禮券，如你對研究感興趣，可點選以下報名，我們將在一個星期內聯繫符合條件的報名者。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
💰💰 Investigating a New Intervention for Insomnia. Participants with insomnia are invited — Receive a $600 shopping voucher
Department of Psychiatry
Struggling to fall asleep at night? Feeling distressed by insomnia? Are sleeping medications not helping? We invite you to try a new approach! 📣📣📣
Participant recruitment for an insomnia research study is now open.
Acoustic stimulation
is a novel intervention method. Preliminary studies suggest that specially processed low-frequency sound waves delivered during deep sleep may help improve sleep quality. This study aims to investigate whether acoustic stimulation can significantly alleviate symptoms of insomnia.
We are now recruiting participants who meet the following criteria:
Adults aged
18 to 45
No history of severe psychiatric disorders
Diagnosed with
insomnia disorder
(i.e., experiencing insomnia symptoms at least three times per week for a minimum of three months, with negative impact on daytime work, study, or social functioning)
Able to read Traditional Chinese or Cantonese
Study Procedures
Wear an
actigraphy watch for 14 days
and complete a
sleep diary (7 consecutive days, separately)
On the morning of Day 8, attend the
Sleep Research Laboratory, 7/F Sha Tin Hospital
for a full-day assessment, including:
Cognitive testing
Mood and sleep evaluations
Questionnaire completion
Overnight
polysomnography (sleep study)
Acoustic stimulation may be delivered during deep sleep
Discharge the following morning (
medical leave certificate can be provided
)
Participant Benefits
Upon completion of the entire study, you will receive:
A
personalized sleep report
prepared by experts
A
$600 supermarket shopping voucher

⭐️⭐️
【中大眼科】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢
【香港中文大學眼科研究】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢及臨床研究
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系現正進行一項臨床研究，誠邀已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢，以評估是否患有甲狀腺眼病（Thyroid Eye Disease, TED），以及是否適合參與後續臨床研究。
🔍 什麼是甲狀腺眼病？
甲狀腺眼病是常見於甲狀腺疾病（如格里夫氏症）的眼部併發症，可引致以下情況：
眼乾、刺痛或流淚
眼皮腫脹或向上收縮
眼球突出（俗稱「眼凸」）
外觀改變，甚至影響視力
及早發現及治療，有助減低病情惡化的風險。
👥 招募對象
符合以下條件人士歡迎參加：
年齡介乎
18
至
80
歲
已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病（包括甲亢或甲減）
輕至中度甲狀腺眼病患者（已確診或懷疑）
未曾接受甲狀腺眼病相關治療
非懷孕或非哺乳人士
能理解粵語、普通話或英語，並能閱讀中文或英文
即使未確定是否患有甲狀腺眼病，只要曾患甲狀腺疾病，亦歡迎參加篩檢。
🏥 研究內容及安排
免費全面眼科檢查
由專業眼科醫生評估及跟進
所有研究相關檢查及評估費用全免
符合資格者將獲邀參與為期約
12
個月
的臨床藥物研究

📌 報名及詳情
請透過以下連結登記參與甲狀腺眼病篩檢：
👉
立即登記篩檢
研究團隊將與合資格人士聯絡，安排進一步篩查。

香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系
📞 電話：3943 0790（何小姐）
📱 WhatsApp：5632 3683
請註明：「查詢 SAVEMORETED 甲狀腺眼疾藥物臨床研究」
您的參與不僅有助及早了解自身眼睛健康狀況，亦有助推動甲狀腺眼病的醫學研究，為未來患者帶來更多治療可能。
The Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is currently conducting a clinical study on Thyroid Eye Disease (TED). We warmly invite individuals with confirmed or suspected thyroid disorders to participate in a
free comprehensive eye screening
to assess for TED and potential eligibility for further clinical research.
🔍 What is Thyroid Eye Disease (TED)?
Thyroid Eye Disease is a condition commonly associated with thyroid disorders such as Graves’ disease. It may lead to:
Dryness, irritation, or excessive tearing
Eyelid swelling or retraction
Protrusion of the eyes (proptosis)
Changes in appearance and, in some cases, vision impairment
Early detection and appropriate management are important to reduce the risk of disease progression.
👥 Eligibility Criteria
Individuals who meet the following criteria are welcome to participate:
Aged
18 to 80 years
Diagnosed with or suspected of having thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism)
Diagnosed with or suspected of having
mild to moderate Thyroid Eye Disease
Have
not received prior treatment
specifically for Thyroid Eye Disease
Not pregnant or breastfeeding
Able to understand Cantonese, Mandarin, or English, and read Chinese or English
👉 Individuals who are unsure whether they have Thyroid Eye Disease are also encouraged to join the screening if they have a history of thyroid conditions.
🏥 Study Details
Participants will receive:
Free comprehensive ophthalmic examination
Professional assessment and follow-up by ophthalmologists
All study-related examinations at no cost
Eligible participants may be invited to join a
12-month clinical drug study
, subject to further screening and eligibility assessment.
📍
Study locations (by arrangement):
CUHK Eye Centre (Kowloon)
CUHK Medical Centre (Sha Tin)
📌 Registration and Further Information
To register for the Thyroid Eye Disease screening, please visit:
👉
Register for TED Screening
Our research team will contact eligible applicants to arrange further screening.
📞 Enquiries
Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences
Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
📞 Tel: 3943 0790 (Ms. Ho)
📱 WhatsApp: 5632 3683
Please specify: “SAVEMORETED Clinical Study Enquiry”
Participation in this study not only helps you better understand your eye health, but also contributes to advancing research and improving treatment options for patients with Thyroid Eye Disease.

Participants wanted for a Chinese reading research study
The Centre for Sign Linguistics and Deaf Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study on Chinese reading and is recruiting participants.
Eligibility Criteria
Participants must:
Be between 18 and 50 years old
Be a full-time student at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Have normal hearing
Have normal or corrected-to-normal vision
Have no history of neurological, language, or reading disorders
Have never learned any sign Language
In addition, participants must meet the requirements of one of the following groups:
Group A:
Native Cantonese speakers from Hong Kong
Proficient in reading and writing Traditional Chinese
Group B:
Native Mandarin speakers from Mainland China
Proficient in reading and writing Simplified Chinese
Research procedures and sessions:
Group A:
Participants will complete 1 computer-based judgment task and 3 eye-tracking experiments across 4 sessions, with each session lasting approximately 2 hours.
Group B:
Participants will complete 1 computer-based judgment task in a single session lasting approximately 2 hours.
Location
Academic Building No. 2, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (near Hong Kong Science Park).
Allowance
Participants will receive HKD $100 upon completion of each session.
Notes
If you wear contact lenses, please also bring your glasses with you to the experiment.
Please do not wear progressive lenses or coloured contact lenses during the eye-tracking experiment sessions.
All identifiable personal information collected during the study will be kept strictly confidential. Participation in this study is not expected to cause any physical or psychological discomfort.
If you are interested, please complete the registration form:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9ELDNEDkVedp7Fk
Selected participants will be contacted via WhatsApp or email.

An Opportunity to Conduct Research in Antarctica
________________________________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in
China’s 43rd Antarctic Expedition (2026–2027)
.
Research opportunities are available at
Great Wall Station
and
Zhongshan Station
in Antarctica. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Great Wall Station (Antarctica)
Quota:
Tentatively 2–5 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
Undergraduate students
Postgraduate students
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
For student participation, it is recommended that faculty members form research teams with their students.
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 weeks at the station
Entry via Punta Arenas, Chile
Tentative departure between late December 2026 and January 2027 or January to February 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for international flights
Zhongshan Station (Antarctica)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
Postdoctoral fellows or above
Students are not eligible
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Australia aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in November 2026
Return to Shanghai in April 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Australia and from Shanghai
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
mid-October 2026
for loading and transportation to the Antarctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain visas for Chile and/or Australia (if applicable)
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Round-trip flights between Punta Arenas and Great Wall Station
(approximately USD 4,000 per person)
Accommodation before and after station entry/exit
(Accommodation at Antarctic research stations is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
4 August 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Antarctica and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.

【誠邀出席】網絡研討會｜生命最後的安寧：殘疾人士在居處離世的選擇
在生命最後的階段，殘疾人士除了在醫院離世，在可行條件下，能夠選擇在居處安寧離世——無論在院舍或在家，這樣的安排使他們在熟悉的環境中獲得尊重與安寧，亦有機會表達自己的意願。
這次研討會透過探討「在居處離世」的選擇，讓大家更認識相關方案，並了解如何支援殘疾人士在生命最後階段作出決定。透過溝通與交流，共建在居處離世的理解與尊重。❤️💕

[Invitation] Webinar | Peace at Journey's End: 'Dying in Place' Options for Persons with Disabilities
In the final stages of life, besides hospital care, Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) can also choose to pass away peacefully in their place of residence under feasible circumstances. Whether in a residential care home or at home, such an arrangement allows them to receive respect and tranquility in a familiar environment, while granting them the precious opportunity to express their own wishes.
By exploring the options of "Dying in Place," this webinar aims to enhance public understanding of relevant pathways and discuss how to support PWDs in making informed decisions during their final journey. Through meaningful communication and exchange, let us together foster understanding and respect for dying in place. ❤️💕
✨ Webinar Highlights:
① Introduction to 'Dying in Place' & Common Myths
② Practical Requirements, Considerations, and Preparations

👩🥰 Recruiting Post-Menopausal Women with Elevated/Stage I Hypertension for Participation in a Ten-Week Oral NR Supplementation (Market Value: 4200 HKD) and Aerobic Exercise Study :D 招募停經後且患有血壓偏高/第一期高血壓女性參與為期十週的NR補充劑 (市場價值: 4200 HKD) 與有氧運動研究 - Department of Sports Science & Physical Education; Program Director: Prof. Stephen Heung-sang WONG
From: ZHANG Jiaqi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155189512@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
儘管已有指導方針規定的藥物治療方案，高血壓在全球範圍內仍然非常普遍，並且是心血管疾病的主要風險因素。 在中國，約三分之一的成年人患有高血壓，但控制良好的血壓患者比例不到 5%。特別是停經後女性， 由於年齡增長和更年期過渡的綜合影響，患高血壓的風險顯著增加。最近的研究表明，恢復 NAD 水平可能是一種治療方法，能夠改善內皮功能並減輕高血壓患者的血管功能障礙。 NAD 是人體內最重要的分子之一，在調節主要生物過程中起著關鍵作用，並會隨著年齡增長而下降。因此，本隨機對照試驗的目的是通過口服 NR 補充劑和/或有氧運動來研究提升 NAD 水平是否能改善血壓升高/高血壓一期的停經後女性的高血壓症狀。 參與本研究，您將有機會獲得市值 4,200 港元的 NR 補充劑及參與專業指導的運動班。所有研究相關費用均由研究團隊承擔，您無需支付任何費用。本研究不設額外物質或金錢獎勵。
🙌🙌
參與資格：
停經超過一年；
華裔；
符合《2025 年美國心臟病學會/美國心臟協會成人高血壓預防、檢測、評估與管理指南》中對血壓升高/高血壓一期的標準（即血壓≥120/80 mmHg 且 <140/90 mmHg，基於≥2 次測量的平均值）；
無運動習慣。
🙅‍♀️🙅‍♀️
排除標准：
存在不適合參加運動訓練的健康狀況；
子宮切除病史；
正在食用維生素B或NAD補充劑。
🙌🙌
參加方法：
點擊海報或通過以下鏈接作網上登記【
https://forms.gle/ggPtpRDCdes3xuhE8
】；
研究團隊會進行初步篩選，以了解您是否符合基本參加資格；
成功通過初步篩選後，預約檢查時間；
前往香港中文大學汾陽體育館參加檢查；
如果符合參加條件，將會被隨機分組，正式開展後續正式的研究計劃。
🙌🙌
計劃內容：
隨機分組：急步行結合 NR 補充劑組 (NRBW)；急步行結合安慰劑組 (PLBW)；僅使用 NR 補充劑組 (NR)；僅使用安慰劑組 (PL)；
10星期 NR補充劑/有氧運動（根據隨機分組後的內容）；
需到實驗室做3次檢查（第0週、第10週、第20週），檢查包括身體成分、血壓和採集靜脈血；
定期隨訪實驗室領取NR補充劑；
根據隨機分組內容，食用NR補充劑/參加運動班。
🙌🙌
參與地點：
香港中文大學汾陽體育館G02
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
張小姐
WhatsApp: 93741382
電郵: z.jiaqi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[
數據安全聲明
]
所有檢測結果加密儲存，僅供研究團隊匿名分析，您可隨時要求刪除個人資料
[
歡迎邀請身邊患有血壓升高
/
高血壓一期更年期後女性參加
]
Despite guideline-recommended pharmacological treatment strategies, hypertension remains highly prevalent worldwide and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. In China, approximately one-third of adults have hypertension, yet fewer than 5% achieve well-controlled blood pressure. Postmenopausal women, in particular, face a significantly increased risk of developing hypertension due to the combined effects of aging and the menopausal transition.
Recent research suggests that restoring NAD levels may serve as a therapeutic approach to improve endothelial function and alleviate vascular dysfunction in individuals with hypertension. NAD is one of the most important molecules in the human body, playing a critical role in regulating major biological processes, and its levels decline with age. Therefore, this randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether increasing NAD levels through oral nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation and/or aerobic exercise can improve hypertension symptoms in postmenopausal women with elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension.
Participation in this study is free of charge. You will not need to pay for any study-related items or services, and no material compensation (including monetary incentives) will be provided.
🙌🙌
Eligibility Criteria:
Absent of menstruation for more than one year;
Chinese;
Meet the criteria for elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension according to the
2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
(i.e., blood pressure ≥120/80 mmHg and <140/90 mmHg, based on the average of at least two measurements);
No regular exercise habit.
🙌🙌
How to Participate:
Click the poster or register online via the following link:
https://forms.gle/ggPtpRDCdes3xuhE8
The research team will conduct an initial screening to determine whether you meet the basic eligibility criteria;
If you pass the preliminary screening, you will schedule an appointment for assessment;
Attend the assessment at the G02, Kwok Sports Building, CUHK;
If eligible, you will be randomly assigned to a study group and begin the formal study program.
🙌🙌
Study Plan:
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the following groups:
Brisk walking combined with NR supplementation group (NRBW);
Brisk walking combined with placebo group (PLBW);
NR supplementation only group (NR);
Placebo only group (PL).
The study includes:
10 weeks of NR supplementation and/or aerobic exercise (according to group assignment);
Three laboratory visits (Week 0, Week 10, and Week 20), including body composition measurement, blood pressure assessment, and venous blood collection;
Regular laboratory visits to ensure adherence;
Taking NR supplements and/or attending exercise sessions based on group assignment.
🙌🙌
Study Location:
G02, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you have any questions, please contact:
Ms. ZHANG
WhatsApp: 93741382
E-mail: z.jiaqi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[Data Security Statement]
All test results will be securely encrypted and stored. Data will be used only for anonymous analysis by the research team. You may request deletion of your personal data at any time.

Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.

Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation

Complete questionnaires and a brief interview

Collect one stool sample

4. 無腦損傷、癲癇等神經類疾病，無頭皮外傷或感染；

6. 實驗時間身體健康，無感冒發燒咳嗽等狀況；
7. 實驗前要保證充足的睡眠，精力充沛認真負責完成實驗；

http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=813414&lang=zh-Hant-HK

You will need to visit twice: one session for the EEG experiment (approximately 3 hours) and one session for the behavioral experiment (approximately 2.5 hours).

1. EEG experiment: Completing language learning tasks with an
EEG
cap
Participants in the EEG study will receive
transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM)
: This device uses a weak beam of light to stimulate the forehead. It is completely harmless to the human body and causes no sensation. This type of device has been proven to effectively improve memory and has been approved for use by universities and hospitals.
2. Behavioral experiment: Completing a series of language and cognitive tests;
3. Completion of questionnaires.
Experiment Locations: 406A, Wong Foo Yuan Building OR G/F, Leung Kau Kui Building, CUHK
After completing
both sessions
, participants will receive a reimbursement of
HK$500
.

Aged 18–30; not majoring in psychology or linguistics.
Cantonese native speaker.
Normal hearing and vision, or corrected-to-normal vision.
No history of brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological conditions; no scalp injuries or infections.
Right-handed (i.e., habitually writes or uses chopsticks with the right hand).
In good health on the day of the experiment (no cold, fever, cough, etc.).
Well-rested before the experiment, and able to complete the task attentively and responsibly.
No consumption of large amounts of tea, coffee, or similar drinks within 24 hours prior; no intense physical activity before the experiment.
No hair dyeing within two weeks before the experiment.
Please wash your hair and do not wear makeup or apply sunscreen/primer/foundation on the forehead on the day of the experiment.

From: Angus NG

angusmingho@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
PIRLS 2026 Marker Recruitment
We are delighted to collaborate with the Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority (HKEAA) in conducting
PIRLS
, one of the world's most prestigious international education assessments.
About PIRLS
PIRLS (Progress in International Reading Literacy Study)
is a worldwide research programme that assesses the reading literacy of Primary 4 students and compares educational outcomes across participating countries and regions. Through PIRLS, we gain valuable insights into students' reading performance and provide important evidence to inform educational policy and practice.
Benefits of Becoming a PIRLS Marker
Gain Valuable Professional Experience
Participate in an international educational study and develop a deeper understanding of reading assessment standards and marking methodologies.
Broaden Your Professional Horizons
Exchange ideas with educators from diverse backgrounds and enhance your professional knowledge and skills.
Requirements
Currently pursuing, or holding, a Bachelor's degree in Chinese Language, a Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE), or equivalent qualifications.
Passionate about reading education and assessment, with strong attention to detail and patience.
Responsibilities
Mark students' responses strictly in accordance with the scoring guidelines established by the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA).
Work under the guidance of Team Leaders to ensure scoring consistency and accuracy.
Marking Dates and Venue
Dates:
29 July – 7 August 2026
Depending on individual availability, markers will be assigned
2 to 5 working days
. Successful applicants will be notified of their assigned work dates on or before
17 July 2026
.
Working Hours:
10:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. (Lunch break: 1:00 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.)
Venue:
HKEAA Hung Hom Office
Remuneration
HK$1,514 per day
Application
If you are interested in joining our team, please complete the online application form:
https://forms.office.com/r/JetCaszPJ5
Application Deadline
17 July 2026
Enquiries
For enquiries, please contact us at
3943 5350
or
3628 8513
.
We look forward to welcoming you to the PIRLS marking team.
本中心很高興能與香港考試及評核局（HKEAA）合作，負責舉辦一項極具權威的全球教育評估——「PIRLS」。
關於
PIRLS
PIRLS（Progress in International Reading Literacy Study，全球學生閱讀能力進展研究）是一項全球性的研究計劃，旨在評估小學四年級學生的閱讀能力，並比較不同國家及地區的教育成效。透過PIRLS，我們能夠深入了解學生的閱讀表現，並為教育政策的制定提供重要參考。
成為
PIRLS
閱卷員的好處
豐富專業經驗
：參與國際性教育研究，深入了解閱讀評估的標準與方法。
拓展視野
：與來自不同背景的教育工作者交流，提升專業能力。

你是否經常在床上輾轉難眠，夜醒或早醒？你並不孤單——許多人都面臨著同樣的問題。我們誠邀您參與研究，讓專業數碼化治療助你改善睡眠！
研究目的
本研究旨在評估市民對數碼化失眠認知行為治療聊天機器人的遵從性，以及其對改善睡眠問題的效果。
治療方式
· 由專業臨床心理學家及精神科醫生設計的電子化治療
· 完全免費
參與資格
· 18至65歲能說廣東話流利溝通（能流利閱讀並理解廣東話）的香港居民
· 在過去一個月內，每週至少三晚出現睡眠困擾
· 最近四周或以上無需長期服藥
參與研究，獲得獎勵！
完成所有治療及後續測試後，您可獲得高達500港幣。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理聯絡。
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you often toss and turn in bed, wake up frequently at night, or wake up too early? You are not alone—many people experience the same challenges. We invite you to participate in our study and explore professional digital treatment to improve your sleep!
Purpose of the Study
This research aims to evaluate the public’s adherence to a digital insomnia cognitive behavioural therapy chatbot and assess its effectiveness in improving sleep problems.
Treatment Method
· A professionally designed digital therapy created by clinical psychologists and psychiatrists
· Completely free of charge
Eligibility Criteria
· Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 65 who can speak in Cantonese fluently, read and understand Cantonese
· Experienced sleep disturbances at least 3 nights per week in the past month
· No need for long-term medication for the past four weeks or more.
Receive Rewards for Participating!
Upon completion of all treatment sessions and follow-up assessments, participants will receive up to HKD 500.
How to Join?
Click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact suitable participants to provide further details:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants.

1. 影片講解：深入淺出地介紹前列腺增生及前列腺癌的檢查與治療知識。

• 測試方式：我們將以指尖採血方式為參加者抽取血液樣本，並透過PSA檢測機進行現場測試，約十分鐘即可得知結果。

日期：2026年7月31日（星期五）
時間：下午3時至5時
地點：香港中文大學圖書館地下數碼學術研究室
主持：香港中文大學中國語言及文學系高級講師張詠梅博士
語言：粵語
講題一：「故紙堆裡覓靈鳳」
講者多年潛心蒐藏葉靈鳳相關珍稀書籍與文獻，涵蓋早期初版典籍、舊時報刊、親筆手跡、藏書票及往來書札等罕見珍貴藏品。憑藉這些獨特史料，立體還原葉靈鳳跌宕豐實的人生履跡與深厚文學造詣，回溯這位南來文人落籍香江、深耕香港文壇的耕耘歲月，系統梳理其於本土文學建設、地方掌故研究方面的突出貢獻，全面闡釋其在中、港兩地文脈傳承之中，留下的深遠價值與不可磨滅的歷史貢獻。
講者：吳邦謀先生為資深特許電力工程師，現擔任張愛玲會會長、香港收藏家協會高級副會長。其學術研究深耕張愛玲、葉靈鳳兩大名家，同時涉獵香港航空史領域，研究視角獨特且積澱深厚。吳先生迄今已出版專著十部，代表作有《葉靈鳳百二年》、《張愛玲在香港》、《尋覓張愛玲》、《從啟德至赤鱲角》、《香港航空 125 年》等，於2015年榮獲第二屆香港金閱奬之「最佳書籍奬」，為香港文學研究與本土歷史研究，累積豐厚的文獻與學術價值。
講題二：「葉靈鳳的五個美學面孔」
葉靈鳳（1905–1975）以文名世，卻同時是一位被低估的視覺藝術實踐者。本講以五個美學面孔切入——頹美夢想者、表現主義者、視覺預言者、浪漫主義者、文藝鑑賞者——追蹤葉氏從上海到香港的視覺足跡：書刊封面、插畫、藏書票與印刷品收藏，及其與比亞茲萊、蕗谷虹兒、麥綏萊勒等人的美學對話。「美術家葉靈鳳」，是另一個值得正視的文學史人物。
講者：黃念欣，香港中文大學中國語言及文學系副教授、香港文學研究中心主任、文學院副院長（公關及推廣）、專研香港文學及書目檔案，著有《晚期風格︰香港女作家三論》、《起初如何︰香港文學十論》、散文集《夕拾朝花》、《熱風》。

Public Lecture by Professor Wing Hong Chan on "The Liquidity Paradox: Geopolitical Risk and De-dollarization", 11 August (Tue), 11:00 am  - Lau Chor Tak Institute of Global Economics and Finance
From: Rachel Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
igef@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Speaker:   Professor Wing Hong Chan
Professor, Wilfrid Laurier University
Date:         11 August 2026 (Tuesday)
Time:         11:00 am – 12:15 pm
Venue:       Room 301, 3/F, Wu Ho Man Yuen Building,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Language: English
Abstract:
This paper investigates the disconnect between the growing political narrative of de-dollarization and the continued empirical dominance of the U.S. dollar. We propose a “Liquidity Paradox” framework to reconcile this divergence by distinguishing between short-term tactical asset substitution and long-term strategic diversification. Using a monthly panel of 11 major emerging market economies from 2011 to 2023, we document three key findings.
First, contrary to the flight-to-gold hypothesis, geopolitical shocks induce a short-run flight-to-dollar effect, particularly among financially constrained economies facing liquidity pressures. Second, we identify a “Sanction Paradox”: since the 2014 Crimea crisis, non-allied countries have increased their reliance on dollar reserves as a precaution against potential financial exclusion. Third, although there is clear evidence of a post-2018 trend toward currency diversification, this strategic shift is offset by re-concentration driven by persistent geopolitical risk.
Overall, we show that geopolitical instability paradoxically reinforces the dollar’s role as the dominant safe-haven asset, making de-dollarization a constrained and self-limiting process.
About the Speaker:
Professor Wing Hong Chan is an econometrician working at the intersection of financial economics and forecasting methods to investigate financial markets' efficiency. Professor Chan received a BA (1995) from the University of Manitoba and a Ph.D. (2002) from the University of Alberta. He taught at City University Hong Kong beginning in 2006 before returning to Wilfrid Laurier University in 2009. His research interests center around modelling and forecasting volatility and economic risks. His articles have been published in the
Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, Journal of Futures Markets, Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, and Resources and Energy Economics
, among other journals.

The Department of Linguistics at the Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants who meet the following criteria for a study on Hong Kong Cantonese-English bilingualism. The study is led by Xiaotian Wang, a PhD student at Harvard University, and Professor Kathryn Franich.
Participants need to be:
- From Hong Kong
- Proficient in both Cantonese and English (capable of daily communication in both languages)
- At least 18 years old
- Has unimpaired (or corrected) vision, with no severe eye discomfort
- Has no hearing impairments
- Has no language, hearing, or neurological impairments
- Has no speech impediments
- Willing to be audio recorded
Procedure: You will listen to several Cantonese audio recordings and provide responses. The entire experiment lasts approximately 2 hours.
Location: CUHK Leung Kau Kui Building G/F
Period: July 2026
Compensation: HK$230 (depending on the actual duration of the experiment)
If you meet the recruitment criteria above and are interested in participating, please fill out the registration form below. Our researchers will contact you as soon as possible:

xiaotianwang@g.harvard.edu
.

- 無語言、聽力或神經系統相關疾病

- 願意進行語音錄音

Announcements
【💰💰💰$200 Coupon💰💰💰】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study🦠💩🧠📝 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書🖋️
2) 網上問卷調查🖥️：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本🧪：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷📄：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝🧧 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent🖋️
2) Online Questionnaire 🖥️: A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection🧪: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire📄: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures🧧. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。

Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.

Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)

travel subsidy

香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語

全免

威爾斯親王醫院

2）喉纖維內視鏡檢查時能清楚看見咽喉，每次檢查需時約三十分鐘，是屬於低風險的檢查，一般只會感到輕微不適。

https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989

名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。

zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost:
Free of charge
Location:
Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:

Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.

香港中文大學中醫學院轄下診所 (中大中醫診所) 將於2026年7月至8月舉辦「三伏天灸療程 2026」，歡迎有興趣人士於網上或致電報名。「三伏天灸」是於中國傳統曆法中陽氣旺盛，天氣特別炎熱的日子，將溫熱藥物直接敷貼在特定穴位上，以做到「溫通陽氣」及「扶正祛邪」，從而達至防治疾病的效果。「天灸」對鼻敏感、哮喘等肺系病症，以及胃痛、腹瀉、痛經、怕冷等具虛寒症狀的病症，具有相當療效。此外，診所亦備有中藥香囊，歡迎參加「三伏天灸療程」人士配合使用。

https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx

- Academic Writing論文寫作

針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html

An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html

This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html

An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。

(👉👉Earn $200!!👈👈) Recruiting teenagers (aged 18 to 24) to participate in depressive disorder study (welcome healthy people) 📣📣(👉👉獲得 $200!!👈👈)誠邀18-24歲青少年參加與抑鬱症狀相關的研究(歡迎健康人士) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，主要探討運用語音分析檢測青少年的憂鬱症狀。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲的青少年參與研究，歡迎所有健康人士、抑鬱和焦慮人士參加。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至24歲青少年,
除了抑鬱和焦慮外，沒有確診其他精神障礙
能說流利的廣東話
使用智慧型手機（附錄音機）並可持續存取互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
通過篩查訪談後，在手機
連續 7 天
使用指定的訊息應用程式
使用手機上的錄音功能進行數位語音錄音，包括（a）指定的段落閱讀和（b）引導音訊日記。
每天
早上
和
晚上
，在應用程式分別回答4個指導性問題
進行跟進訪談
完成實驗及跟進評估後，可以獲得$200現金津貼。
有興趣的參加者請按以下連結填寫問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_801s3xAKvKm1Uma
研究員將通過WhatsApp聯絡合適的參加者，並詳細解釋研究內容。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。
For participants who are interested, please click the link below to complete the questionnaire:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_801s3xAKvKm1Uma
The research team will contact eligible participants via WhatsApp to explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purposes and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852-53202853).

便秘🚽？嗅覺變差👃？睡覺拳打腳踢💤？有腦退化家族史🧠？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
💪提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
📱中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
🔍研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
💰參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼💰

符合資格並完成問卷者可獲 HK$100元超市禮券💰

部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券💰
📱立刻掃描海報右下方
二維碼 (QR Code)
或

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2

Constipated🚽？Weakened sense of smell👃？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) 💤？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease🧠？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
💪Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
📱Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
🔍Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
💰Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance. 💰
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher💰
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher💰
📱 Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2

邀請參加本項研究
初步證據顯示, 間歇性飲食（INTD）和高強度間歇運動（HIIE）在改善心血管代謝健康和減重方面存在協同作用。本研究旨在探討INTD和HIIE對體力活動不足的中央肥胖成人的心血管健康的影響。
受試者招募
本研究的目標人群為香港體力活動不足的中年成年人（年齡40至64歲），並且具有中央肥胖。中央肥胖將定義為男性腰圍達90厘米（cm）或以上，女性腰圍達80厘米或以上。如果您對任何列出的條件有疑問，請諮詢研究人員。
https://forms.gle/FmCFdyFgdEyudP8k8
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
馬先生
WhatsApp: 39436085
電郵:
sspe.project0716@gmail.com
Invitation to Participate in Research Study
Preliminary evidence has suggested a synergistic interaction effect of intermittent dieting (INTD) and high intensity interval exercise (HIIE) on cardio-metabolic health and weight loss. This study aims to examine the effects of INTD and HIIE and intermittent dieting for cardiometabolic and cardiovascular fitness in physically inactive adults with central obesity.
Participant Recruitment
The target population of the proposed study will be physically inactive middle-aged adults (aged 40–64 years) with central obesity in Hong Kong. Central obesity will be defined as having a waist circumference 90 centimeters (cm) or above for men and 80 cm or above for women. If you are unsure about any of the listed conditions, then you should consult with the researchers.
Contact Us
If you are interested and have any inquiries, please feel free to contact us:
Mr. MA
WhatsApp: 39436085
Email: sspe.project0716@gmail.com

中醫針灸臨床實用技術與方法專題研討會
為促進中醫針灸臨床實踐與學術研究之交流，深化針灸理論於臨床診治中的應用，由博愛醫院與香港中文大學中醫學院共同合辦、並由香港註冊中醫學會、羅湖區中醫院及九龍總商會支持舉辦的「中醫針灸臨床實用技術與方法專題研討會」謹訂於 2026 年 7 月 19 日（星期日）假香港中文大學康本國際學術園舉行。本次研討會以針灸臨床實務為核心，聚焦常見及疑難病證之辨證施治思路與操作要點，透過臨床經驗分享與學術探討，促進針灸領域之專業交流，進一步推動針灸臨床應用之理論深化與實務發展。
研討會詳情
日期：2026 年 7 月 19 日 (星期日)
時間：上午 9 時 30 分至下午 5 時 30 分
地點：香港中文大學康本國際學術園地下 2 號演講廳 (YIA LT2)

Join Our Team as a Research Intern!
Are you a passionate student looking to gain invaluable research and clinical experience? The Sleep Research Team at the Department of Psychiatry, CUHK is currently seeking research interns to support our exciting projects in the field of sleep and mental health.
Why Join Us?
As a research intern, you will:
Collaborate with a dedicated team passionate about improving sleep and mental health.
Gain firsthand experience in conducting psychological assessments and observing psychotherapy sessions.
Have the opportunity to review audio recordings of psychotherapy sessions, enhancing your understanding of real-world clinical practices.
Receive comprehensive training to equip you with essential skills in research and clinical support.
Requirements:
Enrolled as a full-time or part-time undergraduate/postgraduate student at CUHK
Fluent in Cantonese and understand Putonghua
Available to work at least 12 hours per week
Able to commit to the position for a minimum of 12 months
Programme Timeline:
Late July - August, 2026: Clinical Training Period (Workshops and Seminar of Conducting Clinical Interview, Role-play Exercise, Clinical Supervision)
Starting from September 2026 - June 2027, you will be invited to assist with:
• School-based Adolescent Clinical Interview for Mental Health Disorder
• Data Management and Analysis
• School-based Mental Health and Wellbeing Promotional Activities
We welcome applications from all disciplines. Candidates with a background in psychology or health-related disciplines, excellent attention to detail, and strong organizational skills will have an advantage. Detailed information about our research team can be found at https://www.psychiatry.cuhk.edu.hk/sau/home/.
If you meet the requirements and are interested in joining our team, please fill in the following form:
https://forms.gle/r6ACw43mY4e3TVrY8
Thank you for your interest in our research team.

From: Emily Leung
