The CUHK Thomas Jing Centre for Mindfulness Research and Training cordially invites you to the following event:
Scientific Talk
Speaker:
Professor Eric Loucks, PhD
Director, Mindfulness Center at Brown University, USA
Title:
Adapting Mindfulness-Based Interventions for Hypertension Across Populations and Health Systems
Date:
Monday, 3 August 2026
Time:
Registration: 11:45 AM
Event: 12:00 Noon – 2:00 PM
Venue:
KCTCRC, 1/F, School of Public Health Building, Prince of Wales Hospital, Shatin
Mode:
In-person
Language:
English
Talk Synopsis
This talk explores recent advances in adapting mindfulness programmes for cardiovascular health, with a focus on the Mindfulness-Based Blood Pressure Reduction (MB-BP) programme developed by Professor Loucks and his team. The presentation will examine the programme’s effects on blood pressure, dietary choices, sedentary behaviour, interoceptive awareness, depression symptoms, and overall cardiovascular health.
These findings, disseminated in journals such as the Journal of the American Heart Association, JAMA Network Open, and Health Psychology, represent an important step forward in understanding mindfulness-based approaches to both cardiovascular and mental health, as well as the intersection between the two.
About the Speaker
Professor Eric Loucks is a leading expert in the study of mindfulness and health. He is the author of
The Mindful College Student
and has led multiple NIH-funded randomized controlled trials evaluating mindfulness interventions in clinical and community settings

From: Emily Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
emilyleung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Where Rigorous Science Meets Daily Well-Being
Public Talk and One-Day Mindfulness Retreat with Prof. Eric Loucks
This summer, CUHK is honoured to welcome Professor Eric Loucks, Director of the Mindfulness Center at Brown University, for two inspiring mindfulness events designed to help you feel better, think clearer, and live healthier.
If you want to reduce stress, build healthier habits, and learn how mindfulness can support real-world well-being, these sessions offer evidence-based insights and practical tools you can start using immediately.
Public Talk: The Power of Mindfulness in Health Behaviour Change
Date: 31 July 2026 (Friday)
Time: 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM
Venue: JCSPHPC, CUHK
Discover how mindfulness can help people eat better, move more, sit less, and manage weight more effectively. Professor Loucks will share findings from his NIH-funded programmes, including MB-BP and MB-College, and explain how mindfulness supports lasting health behaviour change.
You will gain:
• Practical strategies to support healthier daily habits
• Insights into the science behind behaviour change
• A better understanding of how mindfulness affects both mind and body
• A chance to experience guided mindfulness practice
One-Day Retreat: Transforming Health—From Personal Well-Being to Public Health
Date: 1 August 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Venue: JCSPHPC, CUHK
Join an immersive full-day retreat combining mindfulness practice with the latest scientific evidence. This retreat is grounded in the nine interrelated contemplative steps — mindfulness, curiosity, energy/courage, ease, joy, concentration, equanimity, loving-kindness, and compassion. These steps form the foundation of Professor Eric Loucks’ forthcoming book, making this retreat a rare opportunity to learn directly from the source of this important new work.
You will gain:
• A deeper appreciation of nine contemplative practices for daily well-being
• Insight into how mindfulness can help with anxiety, depression, stress, chronic pain, and physical health
• Fresh ideas for applying mindfulness in digital tools and leadership
About the Speaker: Prof. Loucks is a professor, researcher, and innovator in the study of mindfulness and health. As Director of the Mindfulness Center at Brown University, he leads efforts to advance the science and application of mindfulness-based practices to improve well-being and address public health challenges. Dr. Loucks developed the Mindfulness-Based College for Young Adults (MB-College) programme and the Mindfulness-Based Blood Pressure Reduction (MB-BP) programme, both of which have been evaluated through NIH-funded randomized controlled trials. His research encompasses mindfulness epidemiology, evidence synthesis, and implementation science, with a focus on translating mindfulness research into practical tools that support health and well-being. Dr. Loucks is author of the book The Mindful College Student: How to Succeed, Boost Well-Being and Build the Life you Want at University and Beyond. Committed to bridging rigorous science with real-world impact, Dr. Loucks empowers individuals and communities by advancing evidence-based mindfulness practices that support health and resilience.

From: Lo Eugene

🛌🌙 招募參與跨文化睡眠研究參加者 🌙🛌 (15分鐘問卷，有機會獲得$100現金券！）
研究概要：
本研究旨在了解不同文化背景下，人們如何理解及詮釋睡眠癱瘓（俗稱「鬼壓床」）及相關睡眠感知經驗。
透過參與本研究，您可以幫助我們了解睡眠習慣、文化信念及感官體驗如何影響人們對這些特殊睡眠經驗的理解，以及不同文化之間的差異。
本研究由杜倫大學（Durham University）與香港中文大學心理學系合作進行。
參加資格：
• 18歲或以上人士
• 現為英國或香港的大學生
• 具基本閱讀英文的能力
• 沒有神經系統疾病（例如癲癇）
• 沒有藥物或酒精濫用問題
• 不需要曾經歷睡眠癱瘓（鬼壓床）
研究詳情：
參加者需完成一份約15分鐘的網上問卷，內容包括：
• 睡眠癱瘓或相關睡眠經驗
• 睡眠及午睡習慣
• 感官與知覺體驗
• 對超自然或科學解釋的看法
潛在風險：
本研究預期不會有任何潛在風險。
研究回饋：
30位完成問卷者將於九月隨機抽出，每人可獲港幣$100現金券。
所有參與均屬自願性質，所有作答內容將被嚴格保密，並只供研究用途。
如有興趣參與研究，請掃描 QR Code
或填寫問卷連結。
https://durhambs.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gxhPknKBxTHAQS
如對本研究有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡：
Mr. Lee Yau Wai
dhhl12@durham.ac.uk
🛌🌙 Participants Wanted for a Cross-Cultural Sleep Study 🌙🛌
(15-minute questionnaire with a chance to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher!)
Research Overview:
This study aims to explore how people from different cultural backgrounds understand and interpret sleep paralysis (commonly referred to as the “Sleep Paralysis Demon” or “Ghost Oppression”) and related sleep-related perceptual experiences.
By participating in this study, you can help us better understand how sleep habits, cultural beliefs, and sensory experiences influence people’s interpretations of these unusual sleep experiences across cultures.
This research is conducted collaboratively by Durham University and the Department of Psychology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Eligibility:
• Aged 18 or above
• Currently a university student in the UK or Hong Kong
• Able to read English
• No neurological disorders (e.g. epilepsy)
• No drug or alcohol abuse problems
• You do not need to have experienced sleep paralysis before
Study Details:
Participants will complete an online questionnaire that takes approximately 15 minutes. The questionnaire includes:
• Sleep paralysis or related sleep experiences
• Sleep and napping habits
• Sensory and perceptual experiences
• Beliefs about supernatural or scientific explanations
Potential risk:
No potential risks are anticipated in the study.
Participant Reward:
30 participants who complete the questionnaire will be randomly selected in September to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher.
Participation in this study is entirely voluntary. All responses will be kept strictly confidential and used for research purposes only.
If you are interested, please register at the following link or scan the QR code below:
https://durhambs.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gxhPknKBxTHAQS
If you have any enquiries, please contact:

dhhl12@durham.ac.uk

🟩🟥🟩 HEADING FOR A STUDY ABROAD PROGRAM? EARN HK$120 NOW 🟩🟥🟩  - Department of English
From: Prof. Wilkinson Daniel Wong Gonzales
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wdwonggonzales@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you getting ready to study abroad ANYWHERE in the world (e.g., Singapore, Philippines, etc.)? Whether through a university exchange, summer program, or self-arranged international trip? If you’re curious about how being in a new environment might shape how you think, speak, or see yourself, this is your chance to
reflect, share, and
get
paid
for your insights.
Prof. Wilkinson Gonzales from the Department of English at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is inviting students to take part in a unique research project on communication, identity, and global experience.
🌍
Why Join?
Spending time abroad doesn’t just change your surroundings… it can shift your confidence, the way you speak, and how you relate to others. This study gives you the space to reflect on that transformation, make sense of your journey, and be part of a project that puts students’ experiences at the center.
Whether you’re someone who adapts quickly or someone who notices subtle changes in how people speak to you—or how you speak back—your story matters.
🎁
What You’ll Get
Upon completing all two short surveys:
🎉
Guaranteed to receive HK$120!
(No partial payment!)
Interview bonus:
If selected, receive HK$250 for participating in four short Zoom interviews (30 - 45 minutes each)
Flexible payou
t via FPS, PayMe, bank transfer, or cash (if arranged in advance)
Most of all: You’ll gain valuable self-insight, contribute to important research, and have a voice in shaping how international learning experiences are understood.
💬
What You’ll Do
Fill out two online surveys before you leave and after you return. These surveys are interactive, thought-provoking, and include a short language task.
Total time commitment per survey: ~20 minutes
You can complete them from anywhere, on your own schedule
You may also be invited to participate in four brief one-on-one Zoom interviews before you leave, during your stay, after you return, and a few months later to discuss your experience. These are informal and relaxed—no prep or special knowledge required.
✅
You’re Eligible If You:
Are 18 years or older
Are a current university student enrolled at any Hong Kong institution
Can communicate comfortably in English
Are planning to go abroad in the next 1 to 4 months for a minimum of 2 weeks and up to 4 months (e.g., exchange, short-term course, language program, informal learning trip)
Can provide confirmation of your trip (e.g., letter, booking, or screenshot)
Are willing to complete three surveys and possibly participate in follow-up Zoom interviews
Have a Zoom account (free is fine)
Can receive payment via a Hong Kong-based method
📩
Ready to Join?
Answer the first of the two surveys here:
🔗
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_d0gjJ21rdjOwZ4a
Participation is voluntary and all responses will remain confidential. This project has been reviewed and approved by CUHK’s Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee (Ref: SBRE-24-0757).
📞
Questions?

1155205503@link.cuhk.edu.hk
)  Research Assistant

靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加
We are now recruiting participants to join our programme.
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 現誠邀60歲以上人士參加一項靜觀課程研究
研究將會探討靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群的影響。
很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育控制組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;
iv) 照顧者負荷指數達 7分或以上;
v)沒有經醫生診斷有精神病患或認知問題;
vi) 沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題;
vi)不是正接受心理治療;
vii) 兩年內沒有參加過正規的靜觀課程;
viii) 被照顧親屬並非剛離世;
ix) 三個月內沒有使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間：8月中開始 星期一或二的 上午
地點：沙田瀝源健康院 - 本活動共8節, 每週1次, 每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，及結束後3個月填寫共次3問卷調查及提供3次糞便樣本。
*費用全免*

From: Wang Yuqing
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
niawang@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
您有沒有試過遇到手機或應用程式問題，卻不知道該問誰？又或者明明知道科技可以帶來很多便利，但總覺得有些功能自己還未掌握？
香港中文大學心理學系馮海嵐教授現正進行一項有關長者與智能電話使用挑戰的研究，希望了解長者在日常生活中遇到的科技問題，以及人工智能如何協助長者更有效地尋求幫助和解決問題。
🙋 招募對象
60歲或以上人士
持有智能手機，並能簡單操作手機
能夠閱讀及理解中文
願意於研究期間分享日常科技使用經驗
📝 研究內容
研究為期9天，包括：
📅 第1天：
填寫前測問卷（約40分鐘）
📅 第2至8天：
每日科技日記（約10分鐘）
記錄當天遇到的手機或應用程式問題
體驗人工智能協助整理問題及提供建議
📅 第9天：
填寫後測問卷（約40分鐘）
🌟 參與這項研究，你將會：
學習新的手機功能和科技知識
了解人工智能如何協助解決日常問題
幫助我們設計更適合長者的科技支援工具
為其他長者建立更友善的科技學習環境
為感謝你付出時間，完成所有問卷可獲最多300元
🤝 一起學習，一起成長
我們相信，科技不應該只是年輕人的工具。只要有合適的支援，每位長者都能更有信心、更獨立地運用科技改善生活。因此，我們希望與參加者一起探索科技、交流經驗，並共同建立一個由長者參與設計的科技互助平台。您的經驗和意見不僅能幫助自己，也能幫助更多長者學習和享受科技帶來的便利。
報名連結：
https://forms.gle/TxXVcEKHnHS9JkPc8
📞 如有興趣參與或了解詳情，歡迎與研究團隊聯絡（汪小姐：niawang@cuhk.edu.hk / 39434168）。
期待與你一起展開這段科技探索之旅！
Have you ever encountered problems when using your smartphone or mobile apps and were not sure who to ask for help? Have you ever felt that technology could be useful, but that there are still many functions you have not fully explored?
Prof. Helene Fung from the Department of Psychology is conducting a research study to understand older adults’ experiences with technology and to explore how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can help older adults seek support and solve technology-related problems more effectively.
🙋 Who can participate?
Aged 60 or above
Own a smartphone and is capable of basic smartphone operation
Able to read and understand Chinese
Willing to share everyday experiences with technology
📝 What does participation involve?
The study lasts 9 days:
📅 Day 1
Complete a baseline questionnaire (about 40 minutes)
📅 Days 2–8

Record technology problems or questions encountered during daily life
Try an AI-assisted system that helps clarify problems and provide suggestions

Complete a follow-up questionnaire (about 40 minutes)
🌟 Why participate?
By joining this study, you will:
Learn new smartphone features and technology skills
Explore how AI can support everyday problem-solving
Help us design technology support tools that better meet older adults’ needs

Participants who complete all surveys will receive up to HKD300 as compensation for their time and participation
🤝 Learning and Growing Together
We believe technology should be accessible to everyone. With the right support, older adults can confidently and independently use technology to improve their daily lives.
This study is not only about research—it is also about learning together. We hope to work with older adults as partners in developing future technology support tools and an online community where older adults can share experiences and help one another.

【誠邀出席】網絡研討會｜生命最後的安寧：殘疾人士在居處離世的選擇
在生命最後的階段，殘疾人士除了在醫院離世，在可行條件下，能夠選擇在居處安寧離世——無論在院舍或在家，這樣的安排使他們在熟悉的環境中獲得尊重與安寧，亦有機會表達自己的意願。
這次研討會透過探討「在居處離世」的選擇，讓大家更認識相關方案，並了解如何支援殘疾人士在生命最後階段作出決定。透過溝通與交流，共建在居處離世的理解與尊重。❤️

[Invitation] Webinar | Peace at Journey's End: 'Dying in Place' Options for Persons with Disabilities
In the final stages of life, besides hospital care, Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) can also choose to pass away peacefully in their place of residence under feasible circumstances. Whether in a residential care home or at home, such an arrangement allows them to receive respect and tranquility in a familiar environment, while granting them the precious opportunity to express their own wishes.
By exploring the options of "Dying in Place," this webinar aims to enhance public understanding of relevant pathways and discuss how to support PWDs in making informed decisions during their final journey. Through meaningful communication and exchange, let us together foster understanding and respect for dying in place. ❤️

① Introduction to 'Dying in Place' & Common Myths

研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。

Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.

📣 [Tired of Nightmares and Insomnia?] Join Our Free Online Treatment Study 📣【成日發惡夢又瞓唔著？】全新網上治療研究，6周助你重拾安睡 - Department of psychiatry
From: Reyane Ao
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
您是否正飽受
惡夢
與
失眠
的雙重困擾，覺得身心俱疲？
反覆的惡夢有機會加劇失眠問題，導致日頭精神大打折扣。
我們誠邀您參與一項
【網上認知行為療法治療噩夢與失眠共病】臨床研究
。本研究旨在評估一項手機應用程式的自助式網上療程，學習有效改善睡眠、減少惡夢的心理療法。
您的參與不僅有機會能幫助自己重獲優質睡眠，更能推動睡眠醫學的發展，為有同樣困擾的人士帶來新的證據。
🙋
我們正在招募
年齡介乎 18 至 64 歲
同時受失眠及惡夢問題困擾
能閱讀繁體中文並以粵語溝通
📝
研究內容包括
臨床訪談及問卷篩查
為期6周網上認知行為治療課程（每週約20-30分鐘課程）
完成治療後的問卷和跟進評估
佩戴睡眠手錶
👉
參與方法
如有興趣，請點擊以下連結，花1-2分鐘填寫篩選問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dbt7HLJzt16miEK
⚠️
重要提示
初步符合條件者，我們的研究團隊將在
一個月
內與您聯繫，進行後續評估並詳細說明研究詳情。若未獲通知，暫不符合本次招募範圍，敬請諒解。
📞
查詢及聯絡
如有任何疑問，歡迎通過以下方式聯繫研究團隊：
WhatsApp/電話：6763 1454
電郵：
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
您提供的所有資料將會嚴格保密，僅供本研究使用。
歡迎將此信息轉發
給可能有需要的人士。感謝您的關注與支持！🙏
Dear Sir/Madam,
Are you struggling with both nightmares and insomnia, feeling mentally and physically exhausted?
Recurring nightmares can make insomnia even worse, severely affecting your sleep quality and leaving you drained during the day.​
We invite you to take part in a clinical study on an
online cognitive behavioural therapy program for co-occurring nightmares and insomnia
. This study aims to evaluate an innovative mobile application–based treatment. Through this free and convenient self-help online program, you can learn evidence-based psychological techniques to improve your sleep and reduce nightmares.​
Your participation not only offers you a chance to achieve better sleep but also contributes to advancing sleep medicine, helping to build new evidence for others facing similar challenges.
🙋Who we are recruiting
​
Aged between 18 and 64
Experiencing both insomnia and recurrent nightmares
Able to read Traditional Chinese and communicate in Cantonese​
📝What the study involves
​
Clinical interview and screening questionnaires
A 6-week online cognitive behavioural therapy program (requiring approximately 20-30 minutes per week)
Post-treatment questionnaires and follow-up assessments​
Wearing a research-grade sleep monitoring device (activity level tracker)
👉 How to Participate
If you are interested, please click the link below to complete a brief screening questionnaire:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dbt7HLJzt16miEK
⚠️ Important Note
Only applicants who preliminarily meet the eligibility criteria will be contacted by our research team within one month for further assessment and a detailed study explanation. We appreciate your understanding.
📞 Enquiries & Contact
For any questions, please feel free to contact our research team, via:
WhatsApp/Phone: 6763 1454
Email: sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research purposes.
Please feel free to share this opportunity
with anyone who might benefit. Thank you for your interest and support! 🙏

香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式網上自助心理健康療程對改善青年睡眠及情緒健康的成效。現招募年齡介乎15歲至24歲青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 15歲至24歲青年
2. 有失眠及情緒症狀
3. 過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
參與為期6週的手機App自助療程
每週觀看20分鐘左右的網上療程
完成四次網上問卷及七天睡眠日記，包括治療前、治療後、三個月跟進及六個月跟進
全部評估及治療皆在電話或網上進行，無需面見！
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 黃小姐)查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of an online self-help mobile app program for improving sleep and emotional well-being among youths. We would like to invite participants aged between 15 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Youths aged between 15-24 years
2. Experience symptoms of insomnia and emotional distress
3. Have not received psychological or medication treatment for these issues in the past 3 months
What will you do?
Join a 6-week self-help treatment via mobile app
Attend 20 minutes of online therapy weekly
Complete four online surveys and seven-day sleep diary: before treatment, after treatment, at 3-month follow-up, and at 6-month follow-up during the study
All assessments and treatments are conducted via phone or online — no in-person visits required!
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 Miss Wong).

大學醫務處 鄧秉鈞健康教育中心主辦 健康專題講座 – 糖尿病的謬誤和迷思
糖尿病是本港最常見的慢性病之一，坊間流傳不少謬誤，例如「戒掉甜食以預防糖尿病」、「確診後須終身服藥且西藥傷腎」或「注射胰島素等於病情末期」。這些誤解往往延誤求醫，甚至引發嚴重併發症。本講座邀請到香港糖尿聯會代表黃卓力醫生(內分秘及糖尿科專科醫生)為大家深入剖析港人常見的飲食陷阱與用藥誤區，幫助建立正確控糖觀念，積極預防併發症，重拾健康自主的生活。
日期： 2026年7月17日（星期五）
時間： 下午一時至二時正
（十二時四十五分開始入場，備有限量三文治供應）
地點： 香港中文大學蒙民偉樓七樓二號演講室
講者： 黃卓力醫生
內分泌及糖尿科專科醫生
語言： 廣東話
對象： 中大全職教職員及學生
截止報名日期: 2026 年 7月 14日（星期二）

https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/eventlist?id=72
如有查詢，請致電健康教育服務熱線3943 6428。
Health Talk organized by Robert Dan Health Education Centre, University Medical Service Office - Myths and Misconceptions About Diabetes
Diabetes is one of the most common chronic diseases in Hong Kong. However, the public sphere and the internet are flooded with misinformation, such as "You won't get diabetes if you don't eat sweets," "Once diagnosed, you have to take medication for life, which damages the kidneys," or "Starting insulin means your condition has reached the terminal stage." These misunderstandings about the pathology and medications often lead people to delay seeking medical attention, which can result in severe complications.
This seminar features Dr. Wong Cheuk Lik (Specialist in Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism), representing the Hong Kong Diabetes Federation. He will provide an in-depth analysis of common dietary traps and medication myths in Hong Kong. It aims to help the public establish the correct concepts of blood sugar management and proactively prevent complications such as diabetic retinopathy or impaired renal function.

Time: 1pm – 2pm (Limited quantities of food will be served starting from 12:45pm)

- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Ethics Approval
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee SBREC (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk) has vetted the study (Approval ID: SBRE-22-0026D). If you have any concerns regarding ethics, please contact them.

香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
🙋 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
📝 研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
🏥 地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝🙏🏻
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 📞 3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 📱 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
🙋 Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.
📋
Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
🏥 Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you! 🙏🏻

Candidates who are available to start immediately (especially July 4-5) are preferred.
background in Psychology, Neuroscience, Linguistics, or other social science fields is also welcome.

Valuable hands-on experience in psychological research, develop practical skills in data collection and participant interaction.
Learn more about how academic studies are conducted.

Strengthen CV and build connections with relevant researchers at the university.

【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 6 July to 10 July: (1) Hong Kong Civil Service Interview Preparation, (2) Taking the IELTS Challenge: Speaking & Listening, (3) Taking the IELTS Challenge: Reading & Writing, (4) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Application Letters, and (5) Saying What You Mean - English Pronunciation for Cantonese and Mandarin Speakers. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx

The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 6 July to 10 July: (1) Critical Thinking and Argumentative Writing, (2) JRE Argumentative Writing I, (3) An introduction to textual bibliography: the characteristics, category and identification of Ancient Chinese Books (PTH), and (4) Academic Writing: An Initial Exploration of Using Generative AI (Cantonese). These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx

https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html

介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.

新亞書院/清華大學新雅書院 暑期交流計劃 2025由新亞書院與北京清華大學新雅書院合辦，旨在促進中港學生交流。通過一系列學術講座、研討會及訪問活動，讓參加同學對兩地社會、文化及科技發展有更深入之瞭解。
本年度的第二場學術講座邀得商界環保協會（BEC）營運總監梁志峰工程師為我們主講題為「香港邁向碳中和之進程」的公開講座。詳情如下：
香港邁向碳中和之進程
講者︰
商界環保協會（BEC）營運總監梁志峰工程師
日期︰
2026年7月8日(星期三)
時間︰
下午三時正至下午四時三十分
地點︰
香港中文大學許國浩堂 (梅雲堂地下)
語言︰
普通話及英語
如欲出席上述講座，請填妥網上表格報名。
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13735788
講座簡介：
本講座旨在介紹香港邁向減碳轉型的發展路徑，以及實現碳中和的目標。透過剖析由 政策走向實踐的過程、展示整體趨勢與相關數據，並分享最新措施，讓參與者更全面 了解不同層面的成效如何共同推動香港的減碳進程。
減碳是一項複雜且多面向的挑戰，涵蓋多個範疇亦即香港主要的溫室氣體排放來源，包括發電、建築能源使用、運輸系統及廢物管理等。透過本講座，我們將深入探討香港四大減碳策略，回顧最新進展並探討在政策、市場發展與個人層面的共同作用下，香港如何一步步邁向可持續及淨零排放的未來。
主題包括
香港減碳目標及排放趨勢
淨零發電與清潔能源轉型
提升能源效益與推動綠色建築
綠色運輸與電動化發展方向
減廢與循環經濟
日常生活中的個人低碳實踐
講者簡介：
梁志峰工程師為商界環保協會（BEC）營運總監，擁有超過25年推動可持續發展的經驗，致力為香港的可持續發展工作作出貢獻。他為香港工程師學會資深會員、香港環境專業人員學會專業會員及綠色建築專家。
在BEC，他領導涵蓋多個範疇的項目，包括綠色建築顧問、能源與碳審計、廢物管理、ESG策略制定、獎項技術評審、資助項目以及持份者及租戶參與等。
梁工程師同時亦擔任講者與培訓導師，經常就可持續發展主題向不同受眾授課，對象涵蓋大學生至企業高層。他的技術專長與策略視野，有助不同機構實踐環保理念，邁向淨零目標。
New Asia College / Xinya College, Tsinghua University Summer Exchange Programme is co-organized by Xinya College of Tsinghua University, Beijing, to foster student exchanges between students from Mainland China and Hong Kong. Through a series of academic lectures, seminars and visiting activities, the participants will gain a deeper understanding of the social, cultural and technological development of the two places.
As the second public lecture of the programme this year, Ir C. F. Leung, Director of Operations at the Business Environment Council (BEC), is invited to deliver a public lecture, titled “Hong Kong’s Progress to Carbon Neutrality". Details are as follows:
Hong Kong’s Progress to Carbon Neutrality
Speakers
Ir C. F. Leung, Director of Operations at the Business Environment Council (BEC)
Date
8 July 2026 (Wednesday)
Time
3:00 p.m. – 4:30 p.m.
Venue
Hui Kwok Hau Hall, G/F, Mei Yun Tang, New Asia College, CUHK
Language
Putonghua and English
For those who are interested, please complete the online registration form.
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13735788
Abstract:
This lecture aims to explore Hong Kong’s pathway towards decarbonisation and its ambition to achieve carbon neutrality. By examining the transition from policy to practical implementation, presenting general trends and data, and highlighting the latest measures, the session seeks to provide a comprehensive understanding of how different efforts can collectively support the decarbonisation journey in Hong Kong.
The challenge of decarbonisation is complex and multi-dimensional, spanning areas such as electricity generation, energy use in buildings, transport systems, and waste management—Hong Kong’s key sources of greenhouse gas emissions. Through this lecture, we will understand the city’s four major decarbonisation strategies, review the progress made to date, and explore how policies, market developments, and individual actions can contribute meaningfully to achieving a sustainable, net-zero Hong Kong.
TOPICS INCLUDE
Hong Kong’s decarbonisation targets and emissions trends
Net zero electricity and clean energy transition
Energy efficiency and green buildings
Green transport and electrification
Waste reduction and circular economy
Practical individual low-carbon actions
Short Bio of Speaker
C F Leung is the Director – Operations at the Business Environment Council (BEC). With over 25 years of experience, he has played a pivotal role in advancing sustainability across Hong Kong. He is a Fellow Member of the Hong Kong Institution of Engineers, a Professional Member of Hong Kong Institute of Environmental Professionals, and a member of the Green Building Faculty.
At BEC, CF oversees a broad portfolio of projects covering green building consultancy, energy and carbon auditing, waste management, ESG strategy development, award and funding programs, and stakeholder engagement.
He is also a frequent speaker and trainer, engaging audiences from university students to senior corporate leaders. His technical expertise and strategic guidance have helped numerous organisations in both the public and private sectors adopt environmentally responsible practices and progress toward their net-zero goals.

An Opportunity to Conduct Research in Antarctica
_____________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in
China’s 43rd Antarctic Expedition (2026–2027)
.
Research opportunities are available at
Great Wall Station
and
Zhongshan Station
in Antarctica. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Great Wall Station (Antarctica)
Quota:
Tentatively 2–5 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
Undergraduate students
Postgraduate students
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
For student participation, it is recommended that faculty members form research teams with their students.
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 weeks at the station
Entry via Punta Arenas, Chile
Tentative departure between late December 2026 and January 2027 or January to February 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for international flights
Zhongshan Station (Antarctica)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
Postdoctoral fellows or above
Students are not eligible
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Australia aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in November 2026
Return to Shanghai in April 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Australia and from Shanghai
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
mid-October 2026
for loading and transportation to the Antarctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain visas for Chile and/or Australia (if applicable)
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Round-trip flights between Punta Arenas and Great Wall Station
(approximately USD 4,000 per person)
Accommodation before and after station entry/exit
(Accommodation at Antarctic research stations is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
4 August 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Antarctica and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
This one's like magic! ✨ Copilot can
read handwritten notes, whiteboard photos, printed documents, receipts, forms
— any image with text. Just snap a photo (or screenshot), upload it, and ask Copilot to transcribe and organize it!
📋
Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
"I've uploaded a photo of handwritten meeting notes from our whiteboard.
Please: (1) Transcribe all the text you can read, (2) Organize the content into a structured format with headers, (3) Identify any action items mentioned, (4) Clean up any unclear parts and mark them with [unclear].
Present it as a clean, typed meeting summary I can share with the team."
💡 Why this works:
Asking Copilot to not only transcribe but also organize and identify action items transforms a messy photo into an immediately useful document. The [unclear] marker handles ambiguity honestly — no guessing! 🤓
📷
Also works for
: Receipts → expense report entries, Business cards → contact info, Handwritten forms → digital records, Whiteboard diagrams → structured notes, Printed documents → editable text.
More Tips & Resources 💡
Looking for more ways to level up your Copilot game? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

你是否對語言學習充滿好奇？是否想深入了解語言背後的奧秘？

簡介
中大建築學院將與沙頭角公共圖書館合辦「榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞 及 沙頭角公共圖書館分享活動」。參加者將先由榕樹凹文化大使帶領走訪榕樹凹，認識其當地文化與歷史景點。其後走訪沙頭角禁區，了解沙頭角禁區發展，再前往沙頭角公共圖書館，由助理館長江晉賢先生介紹與沙頭角及榕樹凹相關的館藏書籍，從不同角度加深對兩地文化與歷史的了解。分享環節更會介紹香港公共圖書館的電子書館藏，讓參加者可隨時隨地在線上閱讀。
The CUHK School of Architecture is collaborating with the Sha Tau Kok Public Library to present the “Yung Shue Au Cultural Guided Tour and Sha Tau Kok Public Library Sharing Session.” Participants will begin with a guided tour at Yung Shue Au, led by the Yung Shue Au Cultural Ambassadors, to explore the village’s local culture and historical landmarks. The tour will then continue to the Sha Tau Kok Frontier Closed Area, where participants will learn about the architecture and development of Sha Tau Kok. The programme will then continue at the Sha Tau Kok Public Library, where Assistant Librarian Mr. Alferd Kong Chun-yin will introduce library collections related to Sha Tau Kok and Yung Shue Au, offering deeper insights into the history and culture of both areas. The sharing session will also introduce the Hong Kong Public Libraries’ e book collections, enabling participants to access online reading resources anytime and anywhere.

This activity is a part of "Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story", a project by CUHK School of Architecture, sponsored by the #CountrysideConservationOffice (CCO) and the #CountrysideConservationFundingScheme (CCFS).

簡介
參加者將由榕樹凹文化大使帶領，走訪榕樹凹文化徑，認識其歷史脈絡與文化。文化徑涵蓋自然景觀、傳統建築及民間習俗，帶領參加者了解這條客家村落的發展歷程。漫步其間，可見榕樹盤根錯節、纏繞古屋的景觀，亦能認識昔日鄉村生活、祭祀文化及過往軍旅活動的歷史痕跡。此外，行程亦會介紹近年由不同持份者參與推動的村落復育工作。
文化大使除介紹榕樹凹的歷史與文化外，亦會結合新界歷史及邊境地區變遷等主題，分享相關背景資料及地方觀察，讓參加者從不同角度理解村落的形成與發展。
行程期間，參加者亦可認識文化大使及村民在記錄地方歷史、推動文化保育及村落復育方面的工作，了解榕樹凹近年的轉變與發展。行程亦將途經沙頭角墟，簡介其歷史背景及與周邊鄉村的關係。
Participants will be guided by Yung Shue Au Cultural Ambassadors along the Yung Shue Au Cultural Trail to learn about the village’s history and cultural heritage. The trail features natural landscapes, traditional architecture, and local customs, providing an introduction to the development of this historic Hakka village. Along the way, participants can observe the distinctive scenery of banyan roots intertwining with old village houses, while learning about traditional rural life, ritual practices, and traces of past military activities. The tour will also introduce recent village revitalisation initiatives undertaken through the collaboration of different stakeholders.
In addition to introducing the history and culture of Yung Shue Au, the Cultural Ambassadors will share background information and observations related to the history of the New Territories and changes in the border region, enabling participants to understand the formation and development of the village from different perspectives.
Participants will also learn about the work of Cultural Ambassadors and villagers in documenting local history, promoting cultural conservation, and supporting village revitalisation, as well as the recent changes and development of Yung Shue Au. The tour will also pass through Sha Tau Kok Market Town, where participants will be introduced to its historical background and its relationship with the surrounding villages.

Workshop Information
Title:
Neurodiversity in Higher Education: Supporting ADHD and ASD Students in Our Classrooms
Abstract:
This workshop introduces teachers and academic staff to the core learning profiles of students with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), including their strengths and challenges especially in the higher education context, to help participants better understand individual student needs. We will then explore how educational technologies can advance inclusive education and demonstrate practical tools and specific strategies to enhance students' engagement, participation and academic performance. Participants will gain actionable strategies for creating more effective and inclusive learning environments in their classrooms.

Lecturer, Department of Psychology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Dr. An Tong Gong is currently a lecturer in the Department of Psychology at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, providing clinical teaching and supervision as well as professional training to undergraduate and postgraduate students. She obtained her doctoral degree in clinical psychology at University College London. She is a registered practising clinical psychologist in Hong Kong and the United Kingdom. Her work focuses on the development of evidence-based mental health interventions and programmes. She also has extensive experience working with neurodivergent populations and their families.

【香港中文大學眼科研究】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢及臨床研究
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系現正進行一項臨床研究，誠邀已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢，以評估是否患有甲狀腺眼病（Thyroid Eye Disease, TED），以及是否適合參與後續臨床研究。
🔍 什麼是甲狀腺眼病？
甲狀腺眼病是常見於甲狀腺疾病（如格里夫氏症）的眼部併發症，可引致以下情況：
眼乾、刺痛或流淚
眼皮腫脹或向上收縮
眼球突出（俗稱「眼凸」）
外觀改變，甚至影響視力
及早發現及治療，有助減低病情惡化的風險。
👥 招募對象
符合以下條件人士歡迎參加：
年齡介乎
18
至
80

The Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is currently conducting a clinical study on Thyroid Eye Disease (TED). We warmly invite individuals with confirmed or suspected thyroid disorders to participate in a
free comprehensive eye screening
to assess for TED and potential eligibility for further clinical research.
🔍 What is Thyroid Eye Disease (TED)?
Thyroid Eye Disease is a condition commonly associated with thyroid disorders such as Graves’ disease. It may lead to:
Dryness, irritation, or excessive tearing
Eyelid swelling or retraction
Protrusion of the eyes (proptosis)
Changes in appearance and, in some cases, vision impairment
Early detection and appropriate management are important to reduce the risk of disease progression.
👥 Eligibility Criteria
Individuals who meet the following criteria are welcome to participate:
Aged
18 to 80 years
Diagnosed with or suspected of having thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism)
Diagnosed with or suspected of having
mild to moderate Thyroid Eye Disease
Have
not received prior treatment
specifically for Thyroid Eye Disease
Not pregnant or breastfeeding
Able to understand Cantonese, Mandarin, or English, and read Chinese or English
👉 Individuals who are unsure whether they have Thyroid Eye Disease are also encouraged to join the screening if they have a history of thyroid conditions.
🏥 Study Details
Participants will receive:
Free comprehensive ophthalmic examination
Professional assessment and follow-up by ophthalmologists
All study-related examinations at no cost
Eligible participants may be invited to join a
12-month clinical drug study
, subject to further screening and eligibility assessment.
📍
Study locations (by arrangement):
CUHK Eye Centre (Kowloon)
CUHK Medical Centre (Sha Tin)

誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）

目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。

Singletons and twins (both identical and fraternal) from K3 to P6 in the 2024/25 school year
Students’ parents

Recruitment of part-time student helpers -- Brain and Mind Institute
From: Xin ZHOU, Hao HUANG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
haohuang@cuhk.edu.hk
The Brain and Mind Institute is recruiting student helpers to support a research project focused on grandparent-grandchild interaction and hearing loss. The study utilizes Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) and behavioral assessments to quantify these connections. Successful candidates will report for duties at Rm 406A, Wong Foo Yuan Building.
- Hourly Rate: $64 / Hour
- Duties:
Assisting with the setup, data collection, and administration of fNIRS & behavioral experiments.
Interacting closely with young children and older adults, to provide clear instructions and support during different experiment sessions.
- Requirements:
Should be able to commit 10–16 hours per week. Flexible weekday hours are available, but working on some weekends (Saturdays and/or Sundays) is a must.
Fluency in Cantonese is required. Possessing good communication skills, with the ability to speak loudly and clearly to ensure participants (especially older adults) understand experimental procedures.
- Preferred Qualifications:
Undergraduate students (Year 2 or above) with a background in Psychology, Neuroscience, Linguistics, or other related disciplines. Interdisciplinary is also welcome.
Previous experience with fNIRS or Electroencephalogram (EEG) is a significant advantage.
Candidates who are available to start immediately are preferred.
If you are interested, please fill in the form below via the following link:
https://forms.gle/GEC5YrQYLSCTcfJZ9
For any inquiries, please contact Hao HUANG (email: haohuang@cuhk.edu.hk; tel: 95867123) for more information.
大腦與認知研究所（The Brain and Mind Institute，BMI）現正招聘學生助理，以協助一項關於有關「祖孫互動與聽力損失」的學術研究項目。本研究採用功能性近紅外光譜成像技術 （fNIRS）及其他行為評估，旨在量化祖孫互動與聽力損失之間的聯繫。獲聘者將會在王福元樓 406A 室值勤。
- 時薪：$64 / 每小時
- 工作職責：
協助 fNIRS 及行為實驗的初始設置、數據收集與整理工作。
與兒童及長者密切溝通，在各實驗階段提供清晰的指令與實時支援。
- 申請要求：
工作時間每週需投入約 10 至 16 小時。平日工作時間可靈活安排，但必須能在部分週末（星期六及/或星期日）當值。
粵語流利。具備良好的溝通技巧。説話清晰、響亮，以確保被試（尤其長者）可充分理解實驗流程。
- 優先考慮條件：
可立刻值勤者優先!
心理學、神經科學、語言學或相關學科之本科生（Year 2 或 以上）；亦歡迎具備跨學科背景之同學申請。
具備 fNIRS 或 EEG（腦電圖）研究或實踐經驗者將獲優先考慮。
有意申請者，請點擊以下連結填寫網上申請表格：

自適應交通信號控制是緩解城市交通擁堵的關鍵所在。本次報告將介紹一種由多模態大語言模型（LLM）賦能的深度強化學習（DRL）控制框架，並圍繞其三個核心演進階段展開分享：首先，我們將探討如何攻克傳統DRL控制器在面對複雜路口形態和多變車流時的泛化性難題。其次，報告將引入一種全新的AI智能體範式，該範式將強化學習處理常態交通的高效性，與大語言模型在應對長尾、突發安全事件（如特種車輛調度）時的強大推理能力完美結合。第三，我們將展多模態框架 VLMLight，它實現了「視覺感知」與「語言決策」的深度融合，有效降低了系統的決策信息損耗。最後，本次報告還將介紹專為複雜交通管理任務打造的多模態仿真平台及配套數據集 TranSimHub，以期進一步釋放大模型在智能交通領域的潛力。
講者簡介：
王茂南博士，現任香港中文大學（CUHK）博士後研究員。他本科與碩士畢業於北京郵電大學，後於香港中文大學（深圳）取得博士學位。
王茂南的研究長期聚焦於智能交通系統（ITS）與車聯網技術前沿，多項核心研究成果發表在 NeurIPS、ICML、IEEE T-ITS、IEEE T-VT 等人工智能與交通領域的國際頂級會議及權威期刊上。在深耕學術的同時，王茂南也具備豐富的產研結合經驗，曾先後在滴滴出行、商湯科技、上海人工智慧實驗室及諾基亞貝爾實驗室等知名機構參與研發工作。此外，王博士在多項頂尖AI賽事中屢獲佳績，曾斬獲琶洲算法大賽及騰訊開悟全球人工智能競賽的最高獎項。
New Asia College / Xinya College, Tsinghua University Summer Exchange Programme is co-organized by Xinya College of Tsinghua University, Beijing, to foster student exchanges between students from Mainland China and Hong Kong. Through a series of academic lectures, seminars and visiting activities, the participants will gain a deeper understanding of the social, cultural and technological development of the two places.
As the first public lecture of the programme this year, Dr. Wang Maonan, Postdoctoral Researcher of the Department of Mechanical and Automation Engineering, CUHK, is invited to deliver a public lecture, titled “A Multi-modal LLM-Augmented Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Adaptive Traffic Signal Control". Details are as follows:
A Multi-modal LLM-Augmented Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Adaptive Traffic Signal Control
Speakers
Dr. Wang Maonan, Postdoctoral Researcher of the Department of Mechanical and Automation Engineering, CUHK
Date
7 July 2026 (Tuesday)
Time
4:00 p.m. – 5:30 p.m.
Venue
Lecture Theatre 5, Cheng Yu Tung Building, CUHK
Language
Putonghua and English
For those who are interested, please complete the online registration form.
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13735641
Abstract:
Adaptive traffic signal control is essential for mitigating urban congestion. This talk presents a multi-modal LLM-augmented Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework, progressing through three critical stages of development. First, we address the generalization challenge of DRL-based controllers across diverse intersection geometries and flow patterns. Second, we introduce an AI-agent paradigm that combines the efficiency of RL for routine traffic with the superior reasoning of LLMs for rare, safety-critical events (e.g., emergency vehicles). Third, we present VLMLight, a novel multi-modal framework that integrates visual perception with language-based decision-making to minimize information loss. Finally, we introduce TranSimHub, a multi-modal simulator and specialized dataset designed to empower Large Language Models in complex traffic management tasks.
Short Bio of Speaker
Maonan Wang is currently a Postdoctoral Researcher at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK). He received his Ph.D. from The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and his B.E. (2018) and M.E. (2021) degrees from Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. His research focuses on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and connected vehicle technologies. Maonan has published extensively in top-tier venues, including NeurIPS, IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems (T-ITS), and IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology (T-VT). Beyond academia, he has enriched his practical experience through roles at Didi Chuxing, SenseTime, Shanghai AI Laboratory, and Nokia Bell Labs. He is a recognized top performer in premier AI competitions, winning top prizes in the Pazhou Algorithm Competition and the Tencent Kaiwu Global AI Competition.

崛起於戰前的香港華商鄧肇堅，有以下幾方面的特點：一是出身於傳統的大家庭，父親是銀號鉅子鄧志昂，他個人亦有穿著長衫的習慣，以華人自居；二是他所捐贈的慈善事業數目甚多，因而有「慈善之王」之稱，因為捐贈數目大和次數多，捐贈的資金來源很受矚目；三是他與殖民地政府關係密切，是支持港英友好的中堅，他從英國所獲得的嘉獎也甚多。是次演講將利用新近公開的檔案，討論鄧肇堅爵士在身後如何在中英兩國展開香港前途問題談判的重要時刻，繼續支持港英友好。

李培德教授現為華僑大學華僑華人與區域國別研究院特聘教授，曾任香港大學亞洲研究中心專職研究員、香港大學現代語言及文化學院名譽教授、日本學術振興會特邀研究員。研究興趣包括：中國經濟史和金融史。

From: Wendy LI

香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正進行一項為期8周，以內服中藥(沖劑)或西藥改善長新冠患者症狀的臨床研究，以下是研究安排：
研究對象：
年齡介乎6至80歲；
願意接受中醫或西醫治療4星期；
每星期一次覆診跟進病程；
目的         : 比較中藥與西藥對治療長新冠患者在改善生活質量、臨床症狀和生活社等治療效果和安全性。
研究內容：中/西醫評估*、問卷評估、抽血檢查、服用中藥或西藥等。
*注意: 本研究會隨機分「中藥組」或「西藥組」
研究地點： (a)中藥組: 沙田威爾斯親王醫院; (b)西藥組: 指定西醫診所 (中環)。
參與方式： 若有興趣，歡迎
1.透過以下方式報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13670048
2.亦歡迎您致電或WhatsApp我們6082-2583/ 2873-3245了解詳情。
Research Introduction:
The novel coronavirus has caused a global pandemic since the end of 2019. People are increasingly paying attention to the long-term effects of COVID-19 infection.People whose symptoms last for more than four weeks after COVID-19 infection are called [Long COVID]. The main symptoms include severe fatigue, shortness of breath, heart damage (such as myocarditis), cognitive impairment, sleep disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder syndrome, Muscle pain, decreased concentration, headache, impaired taste and smell, etc. affect the respiratory system, cardiovascular system, digestive system, urinary system, immune system, etc.
The Hong Kong Institute of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine at the Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting an 8-week clinical study on the improvement of symptoms of patients with COVID-19 by taking Chinese medicine (infusion) or Western medicine.
Target
: Age 6-80 who have recovered from COVID-19 infection.
Purpose
: To compare the therapeutic effects and safety of traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine on improving the quality of life, clinical symptoms and social functions of long-term COVID-19 patients.
Research Content
: Visits, questionnaire assessment, blood draw before and after taking medicine,taking research Chinese medicine or Western medicine, etc.
Study Location
:(a) Chinese medicine group: Prince of Wales Hospital, Shatin;
(b) Western medicine group: designated western medicine clinic.
Participation
： Free of charge. If interested, please
1. sign up through the following ：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13670048
2. You are also welcome to call or WhatsApp us at 6082-2583/ 2873-3245 for details.

Announcements
【💰$200 Coupon💰】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study🦠💩🧠📝 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書🖋️
2) 網上問卷調查🖥️：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本🧪：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷📄：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝🧧 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent🖋️
2) Online Questionnaire 🖥️: A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection🧪: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire📄: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures🧧. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

Dear Students,
You are cordially invited to participate in a survey study jointly led by Prof. Emmanuel Cheung (Critical Care Medicine Unit, University of Hong Kong) and Dr. Ann Lau (Centre for Bioethics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong).
As you may be aware, the Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance will come into effect on 31 July 2026. This study seeks to explore medical students’ knowledge and preparedness to engage in advance care planning and end-of-life discussions.
The survey is anonymous, and participation is entirely voluntary. It will take around 10 minutes to complete. Only aggregate data will be reported.
Eligibility:
All medical students enrolled in HKU (MBBS) and CUHK (MBChB).

https://hku.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eW35gjGnwzz98iy

From: Tim Lau

香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.

JOIN US for the Service-Learning Workshop

Your Best MAIT
(Modular AI Teacher): A Fully Autonomous Approach to Facilitating Team-Based Learning in Service-Learning”
. The workshop information is listed below.
Workshop Information
Title:
Your Best MAIT
(Modular AI Teacher): A Fully Autonomous Approach to Facilitating Team-Based Learning in Service-Learning
Abstract:
This session introduces "Your Best MAIT" (Modular AI Teacher), an innovative modular teaching method which combines several AI tools to automate complex classroom interactions. While many educators have experimented with individual AI tools, this project combines highly visual AI-based avatars with text-based Large Language Models (LLMs) into a single, integrated framework to maximize the strengths of both technologies.
We will demonstrate how MAIT was successfully applied to autonomous facilitation of Team-Based Learning (TBL) in medical education. Attendees will see how strategic instructional design allows MAIT to independently manage a full TBL class—including individual assessments, team activities, and guided discussions.
Finally, we will share practical insights on how this modular AI approach can be easily adapted to other practitioner-oriented and service-learning contexts, such as case-based discussions and project evaluations, providing participants with concrete ideas for their own classrooms.
Organizer:
Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research (CLEAR), The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Co-organizers:
Centre for Innovative Service-Learning, Hong Kong Baptist University
Office of Service-Learning, Lingnan University
Supporting Organization:
Service-Learning and Leadership Office, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
Speaker:
Dr. Christopher SEE
Lecturer, School of Biomedical Sciences, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Dr. Christopher See is a medical educator, holding a medical degree from the University of Cambridge and a Ph.D. from The University of Hong Kong in Medical Education. Currently a lecturer in anatomy in the Faculty of Medicine, he has received 11 teaching awards including the Teaching Excellence Award from the University of Manchester and the Faculty Education Award from CUHK in 2022 and 2026.
His educational research focuses on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and gamification in medical education, receiving over HKD 7.3 million in grants and multiple publications, conference keynote speeches and invited lectures in this area. He has taught modules on AI and Machine Learning for healthcare in several medical schools. He leads both the AI for Education Community of Practice in CUHK and a Hong Kong-wide HKD 1.6 million TDLEG initiative “AI for Education” with 5 partner institutions.

[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
🙋 Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.
📋
Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
🏥 Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you! 🙏🏻

近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼

Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study |
💰🎁
Earn up to HKD 500
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders

Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.

This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx

【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。

From: Emily Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
emilyleung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Exploring the "Feeling Tone" (Vedana) – A Unique 4-Day Journey
Are you ready to move beyond basic mindfulness and explore the subtle layers of your experience?
We are thrilled to present "The Feeling Tone: Exploring Mindfulness Frame by Frame," a specialized 4-day retreat and teacher training at CUHK. This programme introduces the newly developed 8-week follow-on course for those looking to deepen their practice or teaching.
What is Feeling Tone (Vedana)? Every moment of our lives is colored by a "feeling tone"—pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral. By developing moment-to-moment awareness of these tones, we can:
Unlock habitual patterns of reactivity
Support wiser, more compassionate responses
Deepen our understanding of the "Deeper Mindfulness" curriculum
Who should attend?
This programme is designed for mindfulness teachers, therapists, counselors, and educators who have completed one year of MBCT/mindfulness teacher training.
Note: Completion (or planned completion) of the "Deeper Mindfulness" 8-week programme and the ability to understand both English and Cantonese are prerequisites.

From: Emily Leung

Where Rigorous Science Meets Daily Well-Being
Public Talk and One-Day Mindfulness Retreat with Prof. Eric Loucks
This summer, CUHK is honoured to welcome Professor Eric Loucks, Director of the Mindfulness Center at Brown University, for two inspiring mindfulness events designed to help you feel better, think clearer, and live healthier.
If you want to reduce stress, build healthier habits, and learn how mindfulness can support real-world well-being, these sessions offer evidence-based insights and practical tools you can start using immediately.
Public Talk: The Power of Mindfulness in Health Behaviour Change
Date: 31 July 2026 (Friday)
Time: 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM
Venue: CUHK (TBC)
Discover how mindfulness can help people eat better, move more, sit less, and manage weight more effectively. Professor Loucks will share findings from his NIH-funded programmes, including MB-BP and MB-College, and explain how mindfulness supports lasting health behaviour change.
You will gain:
• Practical strategies to support healthier daily habits
• Insights into the science behind behaviour change
• A better understanding of how mindfulness affects both mind and body
• A chance to experience guided mindfulness practice
One-Day Retreat: Transforming Health—From Personal Well-Being to Public Health
Date: 1 August 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Venue: SPHPC, CUHK
Join an immersive full-day retreat combining mindfulness practice with the latest scientific evidence. This retreat is grounded in the nine interrelated contemplative steps — mindfulness, curiosity, energy/courage, ease, joy, concentration, equanimity, loving-kindness, and compassion. These steps form the foundation of Professor Eric Loucks’ forthcoming book, making this retreat a rare opportunity to learn directly from the source of this important new work.
You will gain:
• A deeper appreciation of nine contemplative practices for daily well-being
• Insight into how mindfulness can help with anxiety, depression, stress, chronic pain, and physical health
• Fresh ideas for applying mindfulness in digital tools and leadership
About the Speaker: Prof. Loucks is a professor, researcher, and innovator in the study of mindfulness and health. As Director of the Mindfulness Center at Brown University, he leads efforts to advance the science and application of mindfulness-based practices to improve well-being and address public health challenges. Dr. Loucks developed the Mindfulness-Based College for Young Adults (MB-College) programme and the Mindfulness-Based Blood Pressure Reduction (MB-BP) programme, both of which have been evaluated through NIH-funded randomized controlled trials. His research encompasses mindfulness epidemiology, evidence synthesis, and implementation science, with a focus on translating mindfulness research into practical tools that support health and well-being. Dr. Loucks is author of the book The Mindful College Student: How to Succeed, Boost Well-Being and Build the Life you Want at University and Beyond. Committed to bridging rigorous science with real-world impact, Dr. Loucks empowers individuals and communities by advancing evidence-based mindfulness practices that support health and resilience.

Talk Synopsis
This talk explores recent advances in adapting mindfulness programmes for cardiovascular health, with a focus on the Mindfulness-Based Blood Pressure Reduction (MB-BP) programme developed by Professor Loucks and his team. The presentation will examine the programme’s effects on blood pressure, dietary choices, sedentary behaviour, interoceptive awareness, depression symptoms, and overall cardiovascular health.
These findings, disseminated in journals such as the Journal of the American Heart Association, JAMA Network Open, and Health Psychology, represent an important step forward in understanding mindfulness-based approaches to both cardiovascular and mental health, as well as the intersection between the two.

Professor Eric Loucks is a leading expert in the study of mindfulness and health. He is the author of

你是否經常在床上輾轉難眠，夜醒或早醒？你並不孤單——許多人都面臨著同樣的問題。我們誠邀您參與研究，讓專業數碼化治療助你改善睡眠！
研究目的
本研究旨在評估市民對數碼化失眠認知行為治療聊天機器人的遵從性，以及其對改善睡眠問題的效果。
治療方式
· 由專業臨床心理學家及精神科醫生設計的電子化治療
· 完全免費
參與資格
· 18至65歲能說廣東話流利溝通（能流利閱讀並理解廣東話）的香港居民
· 在過去一個月內，每週至少三晚出現睡眠困擾
· 最近四周或以上無需長期服藥
參與研究，獲得獎勵！
完成所有治療及後續測試後，您可獲得高達500港幣。
