請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理聯絡。
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you often toss and turn in bed, wake up frequently at night, or wake up too early? You are not alone—many people experience the same challenges. We invite you to participate in our study and explore professional digital treatment to improve your sleep!
Purpose of the Study
This research aims to evaluate the public’s adherence to a digital insomnia cognitive behavioural therapy chatbot and assess its effectiveness in improving sleep problems.
Treatment Method
· A professionally designed digital therapy created by clinical psychologists and psychiatrists
· Completely free of charge
Eligibility Criteria
· Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 65 who can speak in Cantonese fluently, read and understand Cantonese
· Experienced sleep disturbances at least 3 nights per week in the past month
· No need for long-term medication for the past four weeks or more.
Receive Rewards for Participating!
Upon completion of all treatment sessions and follow-up assessments, participants will receive up to HKD 500.
How to Join?
Click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact suitable participants to provide further details:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants.

Tutors enlistment exercise for student hostels in Shaw College (Academic Year 2026/27)
Shaw College would like to enlist male and female volunteers to serve as Resident Tutors for the 2026/2027 academic year.
Requirements
Full-time degree-holding CUHK staff / full-time postgraduate students / final-year undergraduate students admitted to full-time postgraduate studies commencing in the academic year of 2026-2027 at CUHK
Fluency in Cantonese, Putonghua and English
Benevolent, proactive and optimistic; willing to spend time with residents
Good at organizing extra-curricular activities and good at inter-personal communication skills
Mature, responsible and energetic
Knowledge and experience of hostel operation, student activities, service-learning programs, peer / professional counselling, study / career guidance, event planning and first-aid skills will be advantageous
Applicants who have previously served as resident tutors with a good performance record will have an advantage

Resident tutors will assist Wardens to discharge the following duties:
Be on duty according to a roster schedule (including Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays)
Provide guidance and support in organizing hostel activities to enhance communication and cooperation among students from various cultural backgrounds
Provide support to general hostel management; enforce hostel regulations and support Wardens and Hostel Manager in handling resident disciplinary cases
Provide emergency assistance to residents whenever necessary
Perform any other duties as assigned by Wardens and Hostel Manager

Volunteers will be nominated as resident tutors. This is not an employment either on a full-time or part-time basis and is not regarded as a concurrent employment with CUHK. There will not be any allowance/remuneration or any other employee benefits for provision of this volunteer service

The resident tutors will be required to attend an Induction Program provided by college
The service period of all resident tutors will be from 1 August 2026 to 31 July 2027.
The initial one-year service is renewable subject to good performance
Benefits to the volunteers as Resident Tutors:
Developing diverse leadership and communication skills through the daily interaction with students from different cultural backgrounds
Gaining practical problem-solving skills in lobbying, conflict resolution and emergency handling, as well as solid experience in event management and hostel management
Receiving training opportunities provided by CUHK and the College

📖 Your Copilot Chat Cheat Sheet
🚀
Getting Started:
Go to
www.cuhk.edu.hk/m365
or use the Copilot app
🎯
Be Specific:
Include who, what, why, and format in every prompt
🎭
Assign a Role:
“Act as a [expert type]…”
✍️
Writing Help:
Draft, rewrite, proofread — paste text + instructions
💡
Brainstorm:
Ask for multiple ideas with criteria
📊
Summarize:
Paste long text + specify summary format
🔒
Add Constraints:
Word count, audience, format, do/don’t rules
🪄
Reverse Prompt:
Ask Copilot to interview you first
🔗
Chain Prompts:
Build on answers with follow-ups
🛠️
Iterate:
Don’t accept the first answer — refine it!
📋 Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
“Act as my personal AI productivity coach. Create a personalized ‘Copilot power routine’ for me. Suggest specific moments during a day (morning, midday, afternoon, end of day) where I could use Copilot Chat to save time, organized as a daily schedule.”
🎉
Why this works:
This final prompt helps you build Copilot Chat into your daily routine — turning occasional use into a genuine productivity habit.
More Tips & Resources 💡
Looking for more ways to level up your Copilot game? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

Join Our Team as a Research Intern!
Are you a passionate student looking to gain invaluable research and clinical experience? The Sleep Research Team at the Department of Psychiatry, CUHK is currently seeking research interns to support our exciting projects in the field of sleep and mental health.
Why Join Us?
As a research intern, you will:
Collaborate with a dedicated team passionate about improving sleep and mental health.
Gain firsthand experience in conducting psychological assessments and observing psychotherapy sessions.
Have the opportunity to review audio recordings of psychotherapy sessions, enhancing your understanding of real-world clinical practices.
Receive comprehensive training to equip you with essential skills in research and clinical support.

Enrolled as a full-time or part-time undergraduate/postgraduate student at CUHK
Fluent in Cantonese and understand Putonghua
Available to work at least 12 hours per week
Able to commit to the position for a minimum of 12 months

Late July - August, 2026: Clinical Training Period (Workshops and Seminar of Conducting Clinical Interview, Role-play Exercise, Clinical Supervision)
Starting from September 2026 - June 2027, you will be invited to assist with:
• School-based Adolescent Clinical Interview for Mental Health Disorder
• Data Management and Analysis
• School-based Mental Health and Wellbeing Promotional Activities
We welcome applications from all disciplines. Candidates with a background in psychology or health-related disciplines, excellent attention to detail, and strong organizational skills will have an advantage. Detailed information about our research team can be found at https://www.psychiatry.cuhk.edu.hk/sau/home/.

(acoustic stimulation) 是一種全新的干預手段，初步研究已表明經特殊處理的低頻聲波在深度睡眠期間出現，可有望改善睡眠品質。本研究用於調查聲音刺激是否能顯著改善失眠症狀，現招募符合以下條件的人群參與研究：
18至45歲成年人
無嚴重精神障礙 （思覺失調等）
確診患有失眠症（即出現失眠症狀，每週發作至少三次，持續不少於三個月，並對日間工作、學習或社交造成影響）
能閱讀繁體中文或廣東話
研究流程
:
佩戴14天體動手錶、填寫睡眠日記。
於第八日上午前往沙田醫院7樓睡眠研究室，進行全日檢測（認知測試、情緒睡眠評估、問卷填寫）, 當晚接受多導睡眠檢查。聲音刺激有機會在深度睡眠期出現。
翌日早晨出院 （可提供病假紙）。
完成整個研究，即可獲得一份由專家出具的專屬睡眠報告 & 價值600的購物禮券，如你對研究感興趣，可點選以下連結報名，我們將在兩個工作日以內聯繫符合條件的報名者。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
Struggling to fall asleep at night? Feeling distressed by insomnia? Are sleeping medications not helping? We invite you to try a new approach! 📣📣📣
Participant recruitment for an insomnia research study is now open.
Acoustic stimulation
is a novel intervention method. Preliminary studies suggest that specially processed low-frequency sound waves delivered during deep sleep may help improve sleep quality. This study aims to investigate whether acoustic stimulation can significantly alleviate symptoms of insomnia.
We are now recruiting participants who meet the following criteria:
Adults aged
18 to 45
No history of severe psychiatric disorders
Diagnosed with
insomnia disorder
(i.e., experiencing insomnia symptoms at least three times per week for a minimum of three months, with negative impact on daytime work, study, or social functioning)
Able to read Traditional Chinese or Cantonese
Study Procedures
Wear an actigraphy watch for 14 days and complete a sleep diary
On the morning of Day 8, attend the Sleep Research Laboratory, 7/F Sha Tin Hospita
l
for a full-day assessment, including:
Cognitive testing
Mood and sleep evaluations
Questionnaire completion
Overnight polysomnography
Acoustic stimulation may be delivered during deep sleep
Discharge the following morning (
medical leave certificate can be provided
)
Participant Benefits
Upon completion of the entire study, you will receive:
A personalized sleep report prepared by experts
A $600 supermarket shopping voucher
For enrollment, please registe at the following link, we will contact you within 2 working days.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ

***
中文版本
***
研究背景
香港中文大學現正進行一項有關長者身心健康的調查，從而制定一個可以測量長者健康生活品質的工具。
招募對象
長者：65歲或以上，照顧者：18歲或以上；
香港居民；
能閱讀中文及以廣東話溝通； 及
曾使用長者服務設施或入住護理之家
參與方式
如果符合上述條件，請在下方連結登記及留下相關資料以作跟進，需時約1-3分鐘。完成登記後，研究人員將於兩星期內與你聯絡，並安排你與被照顧的長者以面對面或 Zoom形式完成問卷調查。
答謝安排
問卷調查約需 10–15 分鐘。首次完成問卷後，長者與照顧者合共可獲港幣 160 元現金以作答謝。約一星期後，我們將邀請二人再次完成相同問卷，完成後可再獲合共港幣 160 元現金以作答謝。每位長者只限參加一次。
報名登記連結
:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3qPvrQNVMFR0vz0
研究海報：
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uT7ZS1Me6Nv_2qnVhXH6MozHA3GMc5mU/view?usp=sharing
查詢
本研究已獲香港中文大學 — 調查及行為研究操守委員會的審批。 (參考編號: SBRE-25-0737) 。如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡主研究員 黃麗儀教授 (電郵:
lywong@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或研究員黃小姐 (Amy) / 張小姐 (Annie) (電話: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404) 。
名額有限！先到先得！
歡迎轉發此訊息給您的家人及朋友！
***
English version
***
S
tudy Background
The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a survey on the physical and mental health of older adults in Hong Kong to develop a tool in measuring their health-related quality of life in Hong Kong.
Target Group
Elderly: Aged 65 or above; Caregiver: 18 years old or above;
Hong Kong residents;
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese; and
Has ever used elderly service facilities or nursing homes.
How to Participate
If you meet the above criteria, please complete the registration form in around 1-3 minutes. After registration, our staff will contact you within two weeks and arrange an in-person/ Zoom interview for you and the elderly participant to complete the questionnaire.
Appreciation
The survey takes about 10-15 minutes. Upon completion, you and the elderly participant will receive a total of HK$160 cash as a token of appreciation. You and the elderly participant will also be invited to take the same follow-up survey in around one week, and you will receive an additional HK$160 cash after finishing it. Each elderly participant may only participate once.
Registration L
ink:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3qPvrQNVMFR0vz0
Study
Poster:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uT7ZS1Me6Nv_2qnVhXH6MozHA3GMc5mU/view?usp=sharing
Contact Us
This study has been approved by the Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee (Ref: SBRE-25-0737). Should you have any enquiries, please contact the Principal Investigator Prof. Eliza Wong (E-mail: lywong@cuhk.edu.hk) or researchers Ms. Amy Wong or Ms. Annie Cheung (Tel: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404).
Limited quotas only! First come, first served!
Feel free to share this invitation with your family and friends!

From: Reimagining Yung Shue Au
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「重塑榕樹凹：共創山海村落」— 地方營造大使招募
中文大學建築學院現正推動一項以「鄉郊地方營造（Rural Placemaking）」為核心的鄉村學堂及暑期工作坊，誠邀熱愛香港鄉郊文化、樂於親身參與實作的你，一同走進榕樹凹，參與村落景觀的復育與共創行動。
計劃期間，我們將邀請香港建造學院團隊擔任導師，帶領參加者學習傳統建造工藝及鄉郊實踐技術。參加者可自選出席一天或多天工作坊。若完成九天的工作坊後，參加者將獲頒由中文大學建築學院及香港建造學院簽發之服務證書，以作嘉許。
榕樹凹介紹：
榕樹凹位於新界東北端，於三百多年前開基立村，是一條歷史悠久的客家溫姓村落，村落鼎盛時期曾有逾三百名居民。由於地理位置接近邊境，榕樹凹在1980年代曾設有英軍軍營，留下了一段獨特而鮮為人知的歷史印記。雖然村落現已無人居住，但村民近年積極推動復村工作，透過修復祖屋、整理村史、舉辦村宴及傳統儀式，如籌辦麒麟隊；重建社群連結與文化記憶，展現出對深厚的鄉土感情與文化傳承精神。
****************************************
願景
共創鄉郊地方營造：以低碳修復與地方記憶，重塑山海景觀。
空間實作：以小型建設改善路徑與休憩空間。
感官敘事：將歷史轉化為具體的景觀導覽。
​共創行動：透過行動連結設計思考與鄉村振興。
****************************************
活動地點： 新界沙頭角榕樹凹村
****************************************
活動形式及階段:
鄉村導賞：認識榕樹凹村落歷史，了解鄉郊地方營造與文化地景。
物資收集：在山海與村落之間收集可用材料。
景觀實踐*：進行場地清理及空間建設實作，由香港建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂，教授鄉郊景觀實踐技藝與傳統建造方法。  （ * 代表當日將由建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂及景觀實踐活動。）
6
月（第一階段：地方探索）：
23日（二）、27日（六）*
29日（一）*、30日（二）*
7
月（第二階段：空間實踐）：
8日（三）、10日（五）、15日（三） * 、16日（四） *
8
月至9
月（第三階段：村落共創）
每月暫定舉行4天活動，詳情將稍後公布。
- 參加者可因應自身時間安排，選擇參與單日或多日工作坊。
- 請參加者選擇所有可出席日期，以便主辦單位安排及分組。
- 導賞活動日期將稍後公布，會安排在平日和假日或工作坊期間舉行。
- 第三階段之服務日子將稍後透過 mass mail 及 WhatsApp 群組（參與活動者將獲邀加入）公布。
- 實際工作坊日期將視乎報名人數、天氣及現場情況作適當調整，並另行通知相關參加者。
- 如出席一節鄉村導賞、八節工作坊可獲中大建築學院及香港建造學院之義工服務證書。
*************************************
活動時間：早上 09:00 至 下午 04:00
名額：每節12人。
*************************************
對象：
* 身體狀況良好，能應付長時間戶外活動人士
* 對建築、景觀設計、保育等感興趣的人士
****************************************
報名連結：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733829
- 如出席一節鄉村導賞、八日工作坊可獲中大建築學院及香港建造學院之義工服務證書。
****************************************
計劃名稱：
「重塑榕樹凹故事：透過實驗式社區場地及自然文化徑共創鄉郊地方營造」
合辦機構：
中文大學建築學院
香港建造學院
榕樹凹村
資助：
環境及生態局環境科 鄉郊保育辦公室「鄉郊保育資助計劃」
****************************************
備註：
1. 榕樹凹屬禁區範圍，參加者需預先申請禁區許可證方可前往。
2. 在項目進行期間，所有與工作坊相關的船程費用將由計劃負責安排及資助。參加者需要自行安排陸路交通，並準備足夠食物（午餐）和飲用水。
3. 工作坊將以粵語進行。
4. 工作坊內容或會因天氣、路況、項目進度，以及參加者或工作人員身體狀況而作臨時調整，恕不另行通知，敬請留意。
5. 工作坊涉及一定體力勞動及長時間戶外活動。如參加者有身體不適、舊患或其他健康狀況，請預先通知主辦單位。
6. 村內沒有士多或補給設施，請預先準備足夠飲用水、午餐、乾糧、防曬及防蚊用品，並按個人需要攜帶雨具。
7. 工作坊地點蚊蟲較多，建議穿著淺色長袖衣物及長褲，並按需要攜帶蚊怕水。
8. 工作坊已包括基本第三者責任保險，參加者可按需要自行購買其他保險。
9. 鄉郊地區路面或有高低不平、濕滑、碎石情況，參加者須小心步行。
10. 如參加者未有遵守安全指引或工作人員安排，主辦單位有權終止其參與工作坊。
11. 活動期間我們可能會拍攝或／及錄影以作記錄、報告、宣傳及推廣用途。如你不欲被攝入鏡，請在活動開始前告知工作人員，以便我們作出適當安排。
12. 如有查詢，請電郵至
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
或致電 3943 6520 /3943 6518.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
“Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.
Sensory Narratives
Transforming local history into tangible landscape interpretation experiences.
Collective Action
Connecting design thinking with rural revitalisation through practical engagement.
Venue:
Yung Shue Au Village, Sha Tau Kok, New Territories
Programme Format and Phases
Village Guided Tour
Understanding the history of Yung Shue Au and learning about rural placemaking and cultural landscapes.
Material Collection
Collecting usable materials from the surrounding mountain, coastal, and village environment.
Landscape Practice
Participating in site clearing and spatial construction workshops led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction, focusing on rural landscape practices and traditional building techniques.
June (Phase 1: Place Exploration)
23 June (Tue), 27 June (Sat)*
29 June (Mon), 30 June (Tue)
July (Phase 2: Spatial Practice)
8 July (Wed), 10 July (Fri), 15 July (Wed), 16 July (Thu)
August to September (Phase 3: Village Co-creation)
Approximately four activity days per month. Details will be announced later.
- Participants may choose to join single-day or multiple-day workshops according to their availability.
​- Participants are encouraged to select all available dates to facilitate scheduling and grouping arrangements.
- Indicates dates on which the landscape practice workshops will be led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction.
- Dates for the guided tours will be announced later and will be arranged on both weekdays and weekends.
- Service dates for Phase 3 will be announced later via mass email and WhatsApp groups (previous participants will be invited to join).
- Actual workshop dates may be adjusted according to registration numbers, weather conditions, and site situations. Relevant participants will be notified separately.
Workshop Time
09:00 am – 04:00 pm
Capacity
12 participants per session
Target Participants
Individuals in good physical condition who are able to participate in long hours of outdoor activities
Individuals interested in architecture, landscape design, conservation, and related fields
Registration Link
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733829
Participants who attend one village guided tour and eight workshop sessions will receive a volunteer service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction.
Project Title
“Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place with Experimental Communal Hub and Eco-Cultural Trail”
Organisers
School of Architecture, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Hong Kong Institute of Construction
Yung Shue Au Village
Funding Support
Countryside Conservation Office
Environment Branch, Environment and Ecology Bureau
Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme
Remarks
1. Yung Shue Au is located within a restricted area. Participants are required to apply for a Closed Area Permit in advance.
2. During the project period, all boat transportation costs related to the workshops will be arranged and subsidised by the project. Participants are responsible for their own land transportation and should prepare sufficient food and drinking water.
3. The workshops will be conducted in Cantonese.
4. Workshop arrangements may be adjusted due to weather, road conditions, project progress, or the physical conditions of participants and staff without prior notice.
5. The workshops involve physical labour and extended outdoor activities. Participants with health conditions, previous injuries, or physical discomfort are advised to inform the organisers in advance.
6. There are no shops or supply facilities in the village. Participants should prepare sufficient drinking water, sun protection, mosquito repellent, and rain gear if necessary.
7. Mosquitoes and insects are common at the workshop site. Participants are advised to wear light-coloured long-sleeved clothing and long trousers, and bring insect repellent if needed.
8. Basic third-party liability insurance is included. Participants may arrange additional insurance at their own discretion.
9. Rural paths may be uneven, slippery, or covered with loose gravel. Participants should walk carefully.
10. The organisers reserve the right to terminate participation if safety instructions or staff arrangements are not followed.
11. Photographs and/or video recordings may be taken during the activities for documentation, reporting, publicity, and promotional purposes. Participants who do not wish to appear in photographs or recordings should inform staff before the activity begins.
12. For enquiries, please contact
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
or call 3943 6520 / 3943 6518.

[💰Earn Max. HKD 400-600!] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [為長者提供認知同聽力測試報告 + 為孩童提供IQ智商測試報告] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗 - Brain and Mind Institute

Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. Our team sincerely invites grandparents with hearing loss and their grandchildren for an interaction study.
Participants need to be:
Grandparent: 65+ years old with hearing loss, and no other diagnosed cognitive impairment.
Grandchild: 6-8 years old, and no other developmental problems.
What is involved? The experiment consists of two sessions (approx. 1.5-2 hours each):
Session 1: The grandparent will participate alone in a cognitive and hearing test. (The grandchild does not need to attend).
Session 2: The grandparent and grandchild will participate together in some simple games while using fNIRS (functional near-infrared spectroscopy, safe and non-invasive!!!) brain scanning device.
NOTE: Participants must first complete Session 1 and meet the study's requirements to be invited to Session 2.
What you'll get (Upon completion of the entire study):
For the grandparent: A cognitive test report and a pure-tone audiometry (hearing test) report.
For the child: An non-verbal IQ test report.
Reward:
HKD400 allowance and free parking ticket (if available).
Location:
Brain and Mind Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (In campus).
If you are interested in our study, please fill in the form below via the following link: https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX. We will contact you afterwards if the dyad are suitable.
For inquiries, please contact: haohuang@cuhk.edu.hk
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
各位家長：
我們是香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（BMI）的研究團隊。我們團隊誠摯邀請有聽力損失的長者及其孫子女來參與一項互動研究。
參與者需符合以下條件：
長者：65歲或以上，存在聽力損失，且無其他已知認知障礙症狀。
孩童：6-8歲，且無其他已知發展問題。
實驗內容：本實驗共分為兩節（每節約1.5至2小時）：
第一節：長者將獨自參與一項認知及聽力檢測（當日孫子女無需到場）
第二節：長者將與孫子女一同進行簡單遊戲，期間我們將使用安全且非侵入性的「近紅外光譜儀」（fNIRS）進行腦部掃描。
請注意：參與者必須先完成第一節的實驗，且結果符合研究要求，方會獲邀參與第二節的實驗。
完成整個實驗後，您可獲得：
給長者：一份認知能力測試報告及一份純音聽力測試報告
給孩童：一份非語言智商測試報告
報酬：
現金港幣$400-600，以及免費停車券（如適用）。
實驗地點：
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（位於校園內）。
如您對本研究感興趣，請點擊以下連結填寫報名表格：
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
如祖孫兩位初步符合條件，我們將會儘快與您聯絡！
如需查詢，歡迎電郵至：haohuang@cuhk.edu.hk

🟩🟥🟩 GOING FOR STUDY ABROAD PROGRAM? GET YOUR HK$120 NOW 🟩🟥🟩  - Department of English

Are you getting ready to study abroad? Whether through a university exchange, summer program, or self-arranged international trip? If you’re curious about how being in a new environment might shape how you think, speak, or see yourself, this is your chance to
reflect, share, and
get
paid
for your insights.
Prof. Wilkinson Gonzales from the Department of English at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is inviting students to take part in a unique research project on communication, identity, and global experience.
🌍
Why Join?
Spending time abroad doesn’t just change your surroundings… it can shift your confidence, the way you speak, and how you relate to others. This study gives you the space to reflect on that transformation, make sense of your journey, and be part of a project that puts students’ experiences at the center.
Whether you’re someone who adapts quickly or someone who notices subtle changes in how people speak to you—or how you speak back—your story matters.
🎁
What You’ll Get
Upon completing all two short surveys:
🎉
Guaranteed to receive HK$120!
(No partial payment!)
Interview bonus:
If selected, receive HK$250 for participating in four short Zoom interviews (30 - 45 minutes each)
Flexible payou
t via FPS, PayMe, bank transfer, or cash (if arranged in advance)
Most of all: You’ll gain valuable self-insight, contribute to important research, and have a voice in shaping how international learning experiences are understood.
💬
What You’ll Do
Fill out two online surveys before you leave and after you return. These surveys are interactive, thought-provoking, and include a short language task.
Total time commitment per survey: ~20 minutes
You can complete them from anywhere, on your own schedule
You may also be invited to participate in four brief one-on-one Zoom interviews before you leave, during your stay, after you return, and a few months later to discuss your experience. These are informal and relaxed—no prep or special knowledge required.
✅
You’re Eligible If You:
Are 18 years or older
Are a current university student enrolled at any Hong Kong institution
Can communicate comfortably in English
Are planning to go abroad in the next 1 to 4 months for a minimum of 2 weeks and up to 4 months (e.g., exchange, short-term course, language program, informal learning trip)
Can provide confirmation of your trip (e.g., letter, booking, or screenshot)
Are willing to complete three surveys and possibly participate in follow-up Zoom interviews
Have a Zoom account (free is fine)
Can receive payment via a Hong Kong-based method
📩

Participation is voluntary and all responses will remain confidential. This project has been reviewed and approved by CUHK’s Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee (Ref: SBRE-24-0757).

From: Lo Eugene
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
eugenelo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
🛌🌙 招募參與跨文化睡眠研究參加者 🌙🛌 (15分鐘問卷，有機會獲得$100現金券！）
研究概要：
本研究旨在了解不同文化背景下，人們如何理解及詮釋睡眠癱瘓（俗稱「鬼壓床」）及相關睡眠感知經驗。
透過參與本研究，您可以幫助我們了解睡眠習慣、文化信念及感官體驗如何影響人們對這些特殊睡眠經驗的理解，以及不同文化之間的差異。
本研究由杜倫大學（Durham University）與香港中文大學心理學系合作進行。
參加資格：
• 18歲或以上人士
• 現為英國或香港的大學生
• 具基本閱讀英文的能力
• 沒有神經系統疾病（例如癲癇）
• 沒有藥物或酒精濫用問題
• 不需要曾經歷睡眠癱瘓（鬼壓床）
研究詳情：
參加者需完成一份約15分鐘的網上問卷，內容包括：
• 睡眠癱瘓或相關睡眠經驗
• 睡眠及午睡習慣
• 感官與知覺體驗
• 對超自然或科學解釋的看法
潛在風險：
本研究預期不會有任何潛在風險。
研究回饋：
30位完成問卷者將於九月隨機抽出，每人可獲港幣$100現金券。
所有參與均屬自願性質，所有作答內容將被嚴格保密，並只供研究用途。
如有興趣參與研究，請掃描 QR Code
或填寫問卷連結。
https://durhambs.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gxhPknKBxTHAQS
如對本研究有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡：
Mr. Lee Yau Wai
dhhl12@durham.ac.uk
🛌🌙 Participants Wanted for a Cross-Cultural Sleep Study 🌙🛌
(15-minute questionnaire with a chance to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher!)
Research Overview:
This study aims to explore how people from different cultural backgrounds understand and interpret sleep paralysis (commonly referred to as the “Sleep Paralysis Demon” or “Ghost Oppression”) and related sleep-related perceptual experiences.
By participating in this study, you can help us better understand how sleep habits, cultural beliefs, and sensory experiences influence people’s interpretations of these unusual sleep experiences across cultures.
This research is conducted collaboratively by Durham University and the Department of Psychology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Eligibility:
• Aged 18 or above
• Currently a university student in the UK or Hong Kong
• Able to read English
• No neurological disorders (e.g. epilepsy)
• No drug or alcohol abuse problems
• You do not need to have experienced sleep paralysis before
Study Details:
Participants will complete an online questionnaire that takes approximately 15 minutes. The questionnaire includes:
• Sleep paralysis or related sleep experiences
• Sleep and napping habits
• Sensory and perceptual experiences
• Beliefs about supernatural or scientific explanations
Potential risk:
No potential risks are anticipated in the study.
Participant Reward:
30 participants who complete the questionnaire will be randomly selected in September to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher.
Participation in this study is entirely voluntary. All responses will be kept strictly confidential and used for research purposes only.
If you are interested, please register at the following link or scan the QR code below:
https://durhambs.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gxhPknKBxTHAQS
If you have any enquiries, please contact:

dhhl12@durham.ac.uk

【誠邀出席】網絡研討會｜生命最後的安寧：殘疾人士在居處離世的選擇
在生命最後的階段，殘疾人士除了在醫院離世，在可行情況下，亦能選擇在居處安寧離世——無論是在院舍或在家，這樣的安排能夠讓他們在熟悉的環境中獲得尊重與安寧，並有機會表達自己的意願。
是次研討會透過探討「在居處離世」的選擇，讓大家更認識相關方案，並了解如何支援殘疾人士在生命最後階段作出決定。透過溝通與交流，共建在居處離世的理解與尊重。❤️

① 什麼是「在居處離世」及常見迷思

[Invitation] Webinar | Peace at Journey's End: 'Dying in Place' Options for Persons with Disabilities
In the final stages of life, besides hospital care, Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) can also choose to pass away peacefully in their place of residence under feasible circumstances. Whether in a residential care home or at home, such an arrangement allows them to receive respect and tranquility in a familiar environment, while granting them the precious opportunity to express their own wishes.
By exploring the options of "Dying in Place," this webinar aims to enhance public understanding of relevant pathways and discuss how to support PWDs in making informed decisions during their final journey. Through meaningful communication and exchange, let us together foster understanding and respect for dying in place. ❤️
💡 Webinar Highlights:
① Introduction to 'Dying in Place' & Common Myths
② Practical Requirements, Considerations, and Preparations
③ Facilitating and Supporting PWDs to Express Their Palliative Care Choices & Wishes
④ Local Case Sharing

我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：

聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:

大學醫務處 鄧秉鈞健康教育中心主辦 健康專題講座 – 糖尿病的謬誤和迷思
糖尿病是本港最常見的慢性病之一，坊間流傳不少謬誤，例如「戒掉甜食以預防糖尿病」、「確診後須終身服藥且西藥傷腎」或「注射胰島素等於病情末期」。這些誤解往往延誤求醫，甚至引發嚴重併發症。本講座邀請到香港糖尿聯會代表黃卓力醫生(內分秘及糖尿科專科醫生)為大家深入剖析港人常見的飲食陷阱與用藥誤區，幫助建立正確控糖觀念，積極預防併發症，重拾健康自主的生活。

Health Talk organized by Robert Dan Health Education Centre, University Medical Service Office - Myths and Misconceptions About Diabetes
Diabetes is one of the most common chronic diseases in Hong Kong. However, the public sphere and the internet are flooded with misinformation, such as "You won't get diabetes if you don't eat sweets," "Once diagnosed, you have to take medication for life, which damages the kidneys," or "Starting insulin means your condition has reached the terminal stage." These misunderstandings about the pathology and medications often lead people to delay seeking medical attention, which can result in severe complications.
This seminar features Dr. Wong Cheuk Lik (Specialist in Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism), representing the Hong Kong Diabetes Federation. He will provide an in-depth analysis of common dietary traps and medication myths in Hong Kong. It aims to help the public establish the correct concepts of blood sugar management and proactively prevent complications such as diabetic retinopathy or impaired renal function.

Your Voice Matters – International Study on Discrimination in Higher Education
We warmly invite you to participate in an important global research study exploring the experiences and impact of discrimination in higher education institutions worldwide.
An international consortium of 52 higher education institutions from 20 countries, in collaboration with Federation University Australia, is conducting this study. It aims to better understand how discrimination — whether based on race, gender, age, disability, religion, appearance, or other characteristics — affects the wellbeing, sense of belonging, and success of both staff and students.
Who can participate?
If you are
18 years or older
and currently working or studying at a higher education institution, we would love to hear from you.
The survey is
completely anonymous and voluntary
, and it takes only about
25 minutes
to complete. Your honest experiences will help shape more inclusive, respectful, and culturally safe environments in universities across the globe.

【💰💰 $ 250 Coupon 💰💰】Recruiting Children (aged 11 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and Children's Emotional Health Development Study 誠意邀請11歲或以下兒童參加腸道微生物及兒童心智發展的研究🧠📝💩🦠-Department of Psychiatry  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
oscarwhwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系，連同社會科學院心理學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀11歲或以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生物及兒童心智發展的研究。此研究希望透過收集健康小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，和進行認知評估，幫助了解腸道微生物與大腦發展的關係。
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書🖋️
2) 網上問卷調查🖥️：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本🧪：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷📄：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
5) 認知能力評估（6歲或以上）🧠：評估會於大埔醫院進行，需時大概1.5小時 （附評估報告）
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$250的超市現金券作為酬勞，是次研究是自願參與性質，參與這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上問卷 （
https://forms.gle/ukQcZCEbo9A59zM26
） 。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 9253-4907 或致電 2607-6050與我們聯絡。
----------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics, and the Department of Psychology of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's emotional health development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, as well as conducting a cognitive assessment on healthy children, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A complementary cognitive assessment (with assessment report) will be provided and $250 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent🖋️
2) Online Questionnaire 🖥️: A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection🧪: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire📄: Recording children's eating habits
5) Cognitive Assessment🧠: The 90-minute assessment will be conducted at Tai Po Hospital
You will receive a $250 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://forms.gle/ukQcZCEbo9A59zM26). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.

香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
🙋 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
📝 研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
🏥 地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心

[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
🙋 Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.
📋
Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
🏥 Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
